259.1: Having obtained a new body where does a preta shelter? Released from pretahood, where does he go to live in?
259.2: O king of birds, hear. I shall tell you about the region where the pretas live. Men attain pretahood by stealing other man*s ricbes» by indulging in sexual intercourse with other man's wife or by doing acts of treachery.
259.3: Having incurred sins, they seek for redemption in 4heir progeny. Being bodiless as well as suffering from hunger and thirst they roam about here and there.
259.4: Evr  the captives released from prison are frightened at their sight. They se for means to kill their kith and kin.
259.5: They bolt doors on their ancestors, put obstacles in the way of manes. Like thieves, they snatch the mane's food in the way before it reaches them.
259.6: They return home, stay on the roof and watch the activities bf their kins. They cause disease and grief to their reU fives.
259.7: In this way, the sinning pretas move about freely. Garuia said:
259.8: The ghost torments bis family people through the enemy. While he was inhuman body be was affectionate to his people, now that he is dead be becomes hostile to them.
259.9: He who does not observe rites, has no faith in the
259.10: From the beginning of Satya yuga to the end of Dvipara, nobody became a preta and nobody suffered from preta.
259.11: A woman becomes barren in life or if she gives Inrth to children they die at an early age. There is a loss of wealth and cattle. These sufferings are caused by preta.
259.12: If a person loses faith in religion or if he loses the means of his livelihood or if he feels greedy in excess or if there is a regular quarrel at home that suffering is due to preta.
259.13: When crops do not grow up, though the rains are abundant; when the expenditure goes up and income is reduc¬ ed; when quarrels rise in gravity, that suffering is due to preta.
259.14: When he associates with the people of low caste or when be performs disreputable acts or when he is interested in acts of unrighteousness, that suffering is due to preta.
259.15: When an incurable disease sets in, or when children suffer from pain or when wife suffers immensely, that suffering is due to preta.
259.16: When one loses faith in the Vedas, Smrtis, Puripas, and Dharmaiistras, that suffering is due to preta.
259.17: When one abuses gods, gurus and Brahmins in their presence or absence, that aberration of nature is due to preta.
259.18: When women suffer from abortion or do not con¬ ceive or when children die at an early age that suffering is due to preta.
259.19: When he does not perform the annual iriddha in sincerity and has no ioclination either—that suffering is due to preta.
259.20: When trade does not prosper though he has gone abroad where he lives in separation from wife, that suffering is due to preta.
259.21: When he lives in foreign lands or when he loses position at home, that suffering is due to preta.
259.22: When he refuses to obey his parents and has no love for his wife, is of cruel nature, is lost in his own affairs, that suffering is due to preta
259.23: If the funeral rites are not performed in the pres¬ cribed way, the soul of the deceased (in rebirth) deviates from the righteous path and falb in the company of the wicked. Then Vnotsarga is the only rite to redeem him.
259.24: O Garuda, a person becomes a ghost and under¬ goes sufferings if he dies an accidental death or if his body is not cremated properly.
259.25: O best of birds, when the descendent knows all this, he should conduct those rites which may release the deceased from ghosthood. If he does not perform rites for the ghost he himself turns a ghost after death.
259.26: His lineage breaks either at the third or at the fifth generation. In each and every birth he lives a wretched, poor and sinful life.

260.1: O lord, I am desirous of asking you how the ghosts ultimately get free and when men are no longer afflicted by them.
260.2: How do the symptoms of ghostly affliction decisively vanish? How can ghosthood be warded off lest it should recur again?
260.3: I shall tejl you how the ghosts become free and also how the person knows that he is tormented by a ghost.
260.4: If a person desires to visit a holy place and. his heart is set upon it, but somehow there is a break in carrying out his desire, that is due to the bad intention of a ghost.
260.5: If a person performs holy rites for the redemption of a ghost, he will find his acticms fruitful. The ghost shall be satiated permanently.
260.6: There are certain sinful, wicked ghosts who harass their descendants. But, they too, when propitiated, cease to liarass them.
260.7: O lord of birds, they too, when their time comes, become free due to their sons' rites and they bless their kinsmen with opulence and flourishing wealth.
260.8: The wretch of deluded soul who in spite of seeing, hearing and feeling the depredations of the ghost does not succour, is tarnished with the curse of the ghost.
260.9: By means of japas, homos and donas he should sanctify his body. O lord of birds, if this is performed, all obstacles and hindrances are dispelled.

261.1: Out of greed if people upset the boundaries of villages and destroy pasture lands, tanks, parks, underground drainage, etc., they become ghosts.
261.2: Sinful persons meet with death at the hands of Candalas, infuriated brahmins, serpents, animals with curved teeth or in watery graves or struck by lightning.
261.3: One who discards one's mother, sister, wife, daughter or daughter-in-law without seeing any fault in them, obtains ghosthood surely.
261.4: One who deceives his own brother, kills a brahmana or a cow, drinks liquor, defiles the preceptor's bed, steals gold and silk-garments, becomes a ghost, O bird.
261.5: One who usurps a deposit, deceives a friend, enjoys other man's wife, kills other's faith, is cruel, definitely becomes a ghost.
261.6: One who discards the family-customs, takes to other customs, is without knowledge and good character, definitely becomes a ghost.
261.7: O grandfather, please tell me what those evil deeds are as a result of which one becomes a ghost and what are the means of redemption from the same on hearing which I shall not be deluded thus further.
261.8: I shall tell you entirely what those causes are whereby one turns a ghost and how he is set free after falling into a dismal hell impassable even to gods.
261.9: I shall tell all those things, on hearing which a person is set free from ghosthood.
261.10: He strictly observed celibacy. He observed penances. He was soft-hearted, truthful and pure. He was afraid of the other world.
261.11: He strictly followed the instructions of his preceptor. He was delighted in serving guests. He observed yogic practices. He was free from Dvandvas (like happiness and misery, heat and cold and such opposite pairs).
261.12: Practising yoga incessantly to conquer mundane existence, he subjugated the sense organs. Following the path of good conduct he eagerly desired salvation.
261.13: He spent years in the secluded forest. Then the idea of visiting holy centres entered his mind.
261.14: He thought within himself "I shall keep immersed my body in the waters of a holy river till I die." Accordingly he hastened to a holy centre where he took bath at sunrise. He performed the rites of Japa and Namaskdra (obeisance) and started on journey.
261.15: In this state of our ghosthood we are oppressed with hunger and thirst. We are unable to speak. We have lost our mental equilibrium. We have lost consciousness too.
261.16: We are Pisacas born of our own misdeeds. We do not know the difference between one quarter and another. We are extremely distressed. We do not know where we go.
261.17: We have neither fathers nor mothers. This ghost¬ hood is due to our own misdeeds. We are extremely dejected and sorrowful because the attack is all too sudden.
261.18: O Brahmin, we are delighted on seeing you. We feel refreshed. Please wait a little. I shall narrate everything from the very beginning.
261.19: How can ghosts, the outcome of evil actions, have names? You may have some purpose in view in having these names. Please tell me.
261.20: O excellent brahmin, While I myself took all sweet things I left stale things for brahmins to eat.
261.21: O excellent brahmin, whenever a brahmin begged him for food, out of hunger, this ghost used to run away, hence, he is called Sfghraga.
261.22: This other one irritated many brahmins with sharp tongue when they came to him for food, hence he is called SScimukha.
261.23: In his life on earth, this ghost ate sumptuously, in isolation, the food-stuffs offered to gods and manes in the absence of brahmins. Hence, he is known as Rohaka.
261.24: Whenever a needy person requested him for some¬ thing, this ghost pretended to be silent and went on scratching on the ground. As a result of this he is known as Lekhaka.
261.25: We have become somewhat wise on seeing you. If
261.26: The creatures on this earth subsist on food, I wish to know precisely what you all eat for your subsistence.
261.27: If you are inclined to hear what we eat, O noble sir, listen attentively.
261.28: O king of ghosts, please tell me what you eat.
261.29: Mucous, secretions, faeces and urine together with other exudations, filth as well as leavings of food constitute our diet.
261.30: We eat, drink and revel in the house where people do not pay attention to cleanliness and where they scatter litter carelessly. We haunt unclean beings as well.
261.31: We reside and enjoy in the house where there is no purity and where people do not observe truthfulness and restraint and where outcastes, robbers, etc. join together and take meals.
261.32: We take delight in haunting the house where no mantras are recited, where no oblation is offered, where no homa is performed and where people do not read the Vedas regularly nor perform religious rites.®
261.33: Religious riles —as the worship of deities, observance of Vratas.
261.34: We hover round the house where gods are not honoured, where the householder is a vile wretch, without shame and decency and where the poor husband is controlled by his sturdy wife.
261.35: We enjoy gaiety in the house where covetousness, fury, somnolence, sorrow, fear, haughtiness, lethargy, quarrels and deception reign supreme.
261.36: We lick up the urine mixed with semen from the vaginal passage of the widow having illicit intercourse with her paramour.
261.37: Dear friend, I am ashamed to tell you about the food we take. O piou.s brahmin, we lick up the menstrual blood from the generative organ of a woman.
261.38: O noble brahmin, prefering penance to riches, and engaged in performing the sacred rites, I ask you, out of frustration. Plea.se tell me the means of warding off ghosthood. It is better to die a hundred times than turn a ghost.
261.39: He who observes fast, keeps awake at night and is purified by meritorious deeds is never born as a ghost.
261.40: He who performs A§vamcdha and other sacrifices, makes liberal gifts and builds monasteries, parks, drinking water-sheds and cowpens is never born a.s a ghost.
261.41: Sacred riles —as the sacraments {Sarhskarns) dcsciibcd in the Grhya sutras.
261.42: He who helps brahmins to give their virgin daughters in marriage, according io his capacity, he who enables students to study, and he who accords shelter and refuge to the needy is never born as a ghost.
261.43: If a man takes food offered by a fallen man and dies with that food undigested in his stomach, he is supposed to have courted a foul death and hence, he becomes a ghost.
261.44: If a priest officiates at the sacrifice of an unworthy person and neglects that of a worthy sacrificer, if a man lives in the company of despicable people he becomes a ghost.
261.45: He who associates with drunkards or indulges in intercourse with a woman addicted to wine or eats meat unconsciously becomes a ghost.
261.46: He who misappropriates a brahmin's wealth, or the proi)erty of the temple or that of his preceptor and he who takes money from his son-in-law before giving his daughter in marriage becomes a ghost.
261.47: He who forsakes his innocent and guiltless mother, sister, wife, daughter or daughter-in-law becomes a ghost.
261.48: All these are sure to be born as ghosts—a man misappropriating a trust property, a man treacherous to his friend, a man fond of another man's wife, a faithless man and a deceptive wretch.
261.49: A man hating his brother, a murderer of a brahmin, a slayer of a cow, a wine-addict, a defiler of the preceptor's bed, one who casts off customary rites, or one who is fond of telling lies, a stealer of gold or one who takes possession of plots of land illegally—all these are born as ghosts.
261.50: When the brahmin spoke thus, the beating of drums Was heard in the sky. The gods showered flowers over the brahmin.
261.51: Five celestial chariots arrived there and took the ghosts away, the ghosts having taken leave of the saintly brahmin.
261.52: The ghosts were relieved of their sins after the pious speech of that brahmin. They all achieved the highest region {Vaikunfha).

262.1: What do the ghosts do in their ghosthood? When do they speak sometime? Please tell me, O lord of gods!
262.2: I shall tell about their form, signs and dreams. Being oppressed by hunger and thirst they enter their former home.
262.3: Though possessed of airy forms, they give signs to their sleeping descendents, O bird.
262.4: They visit the place where their sons, wives and relatives sleep.
262.5: If a person dreams of a horse, an elephant, a bull, or a man with deformed face, if a person awakened from sleep sees himself in the opposite side of the bed, this is all due to the working of a ghost.
262.6: If one snatches the food from him while he is eating in dream, if thirsty, one drinks water,
262.7: If in dream one rides a bull or moves with bulls or if one springs up in the sky or goes to a holy place hungry,
262.8: He who begs in dream oppressed by hunger or thirst should give pindas to the manes to ward off coming distress.
262.9: If one sees in dream his son, cattle, father, brother, wife, getting out of house, it is due to the working of a ghost.
262.10: These signs, O bird, call for atonement. One should bathe at home or at a holy place, give water oblation to a deity at the root of a fig tree.
262.11: Or give black corn, perform worship, offer gifts to a Vedic scholar and do homa as far as his means can allow.
262.12: If, in faith, one reads or hears this discourse, the ghosts disappear immediately from his vicinity.
262.13: If, in faith, one reads or hears this discourse, the ghosts disappear immediately from his vicinity.

263.1: As the Sastras declare none dies a premature death. But, how is it that a brahmin scholar of the Vedas or a mighty monarch sometimes meet with death prematurely. Hence, what is stated in the lastras by Brahma appears to be untrue.
263.2: Kali Age. For a detailed account of the concept of four ages, see Pargiter's Ancient Indian Historical Tradition. Ch. XV., pp. 175-176.
263.3: O wise bird, well said. You are my staunch devotee. Please listen to my important words that dispel all sorts of sins.
263.4: O lord of birds, the brilliant son of Kasyapa, I shall tell you how god of death induced by Brahma, takes away the life quickly.
263.5: Evil deeds take men quickly to Yama's abode, if they do not possess faith, if they are impure, if they do not practice Vedic rites, if they have cast off auspicious things or if they indulge in falsehood or if they practise deception.
263.6: If a man forsakes his duties or resorts to forbidden activities or those which are enjoined on others he dies quickly.
263.7: If a Sudra does something other than service to the twice-born he is wasted in any of the hells—bad, worse or worst or as the case may be.
263.8: If one neglects both, Z)5rta, ja/»a, Ao-Tia, study of the Vedas or worship of gods on a certain day that is a day wasted in the life of that man.
263.9: I affirm that the attributes of body evolved out of the morsels of food and lymph arc not permanent or steady or rooted in firm grounds.
263.10: The food cooked in the morning becomes stale in the evening. How can one expect permanence in the body sustain¬ ed by such a food?
263.11: O lord of birds, realising that the body bound with its activities is already lost, people should strive for burning away their sins.
263.12: Body belongs to one who nourishes it with food or to one who generates, father, mother or both. It is reduced to ashes or devoured by dogs or eaten up by worms. What sanctity can there be in regard to it?
263.13: A person should make an earnest effort for the destruction of sins. The sin which he commits in various births is threefold.
263.14: Wlien he takes birth as a human being the sins visit him. When he remembers his past sinful life he becomes sorrowful.
263.15: When he resides in human womb after sojourning in the various beings such as birds, etc., the full velocity of his past actions forces an impact on him. Only after residing in the womb does he realise it.
263.16: He begins to realize the tortures of life, such as anxiety, sicknes.s, distress, old age, deformity and the rest.
263.17: But the moment he comes out of the womb, ignorance envelops him. As an infant he realizes nothing.
263.18: In youth too, he does not realize, blinded as he is by sexual urge. But he who realizes it fiom the very beginning attains salvation.
263.19: From the time of conception itself, death awaits the person whether he be infant or an old man or a youth, whether he be rich or poor handsome or ugly.
263.20: When the actions of previous births ripen, man succumbs to death. From the time of conception to the fi/th year even a slight sin may cause death.
263.21: How should the rites of pinda be performed if a person dies in infancy? What should be done when death occurs in the womb itself? What should be done when the death occurs before the tonsure ceremony?
263.22: What are the rules of obsequy if death occurs after the tonsure ceremony?
263.23: Milk should be distributed according to one's capacity among the children in the neighbourhood in order to please them. After the tonsure and upto five years, if the child dies, cremation should be performed duly.
263.24: Milk should be distributed to children and they may be fed also. The rites of children upto five, on being dead, should be in accordance with the tradition of the family.

265.1: O foremost among deities, take pity on me and tell me truly when the sapinda rite has to be performed for the dead.
265.2: How do they attain their goal when sapinda rite is performed? What happens when it is not performed? How can you say that sapirda is performed both for man and woman.
265.3: How can both husband and wife derive the benefit of sapinda? If the husband is alive how can one perlbrm sapinda for a woman?
265.4: O lord of deities, how in the heaven does she attain the region of her husband? When the sacred fire is lit how is sraddha performed along with Vrfotsarga on the same day?
265.5: O lord, how could the water-jar be gifted, if the sapinda rite is performed already? Please tell me, out of grace, since the welfare of the world is involved.
265.6: Thereafter, he sojourns in the Pitrloka* together with the manes. Hence, the sapinda should be performed by the son to his father.
265.7: After sapinikarana he abandons his identity and becomes one with the manes. The assimilation with grandfather is made within six months from the period the rite is complelcd.
265.8: No joyous ceremony such as marriage, etc, can be performed if the householder dies and the sapina has not been performed. Even a mendicant will not take alms from that house unless the sapinda is performed duly.
265.9: As long as the pindas arc not merged, one remains impure. O lord of birds, the dead man gets a new appellation after this tnerge.
265.10: The obligations of a lamily are many, Man's life is being wasted every moment. Human body is not permanent. In view of this, the twelfth day after death is thought to be appropriate for the sapinda rite.
265.11: If the body has not yet been evolved no sraddha is enjoined for him together with the other manes. If the sixteen sraddhas are performed he is released from pretahood, acquires the status of pitrs and rejoices in their company.
265.12: The woman whose marriage has taken place according to the practice observed in the marriages, such as Btdhina, etc, is entitled to rice-ball and water libation which should be oflered by the dynastic title of'hcr husband.
265.13: According to Manu, if among many brothers in a family only one has a son that son is common to all brothers.
265.14: 'riie sapinda of persons devoid of sons should be peifoimed by the wife or rtviks or the family priest.
265.15: A son whose tonsure ceremony has been held is entitled to perform his father's sraddha but he shall not recite the vedic mantras. He can very well say svadhd.
265.16: A woman's sapinda can be performed by three persons, beginning with her husband (i.e. husband, son or husband's brother).
265.17: After sapinda, all individual sraddhas are avoided. He who gives separate pinda virtually kills the Pitrs.
265.18: NandimiiUia Sraddha —The ceremony performed in memory of the manes, preliminary to any festive occasion such as marriage, etc.
265.19: If after performing sapin(.la any one performs t'ko(l(]if}a, he makes himself and the dead man victim of Yama's wrath. Upio a year the rite for redemption from ghosthood should be performed under the specific name and gotta by the I lo use holder.
265.20: The water-jar oll'cring, feeding, gifts of lights, etc. after tlie sapinda rite is over, should be made in a single unit.
265.21: After the pitula offering has been made, he should gift as much of Ibotl-stulf to a brahmin as would last for a year. A person for whom all due rites are performed shall obtain a divine i)ody and will proceed in the divine aerial car fully contented, to tlie realm of Yama.

265.23: An adopted daughter shall subscribe to her husband's gob a till the birth of a son After the birth of her son she reverts to the gotra of her father.
265.24: If the wife ascends the funeral pyre there is aways the identity of rites for her husband and wife. I'lie.separate Sraddha (ekocidista) shall be performed by the son on the anniversary of his father's death.
265.25: If both husband and wife die on one and the same day, without a child and arc cremated in the same pyre, the kinsman should perform separate Sraddha for cacli. The sapinda is along with her husband.
265.26: If both husband and wife die and are cremated in the same pyre, food is cooked for pinda at the same time but pindas are offered separately.
265.27: If two persons, men or women, of the same gotra die on the same day, the altar for the ritual is common for both, but the offering of gifts is separate.
265.28: The Sraddha performed on the eleventh day should consist of the same kind of cooked food in the case of husband and wife but not in the case of others.
265.29: If Sraddhas are performed in holy centres, in the dark fortnight or during the period of solar or lunar eclipse, the same cooked food can be used for many Sraddhas.
265.30: Just as the impurities of metals are removed when metals are melted in fire, so the woman shall remove her impurities in the fire that is on a par with nectar.
265.31: Leaving off her mother, father and sons she will attain an everlasting happiness by following her dead husband.
265.32: Calculating by the celestial calander she shall stay in heaven for thirty five million years with the stars.

265.34: Hence, a woman shall endeavour to serve her husband in thought, word and action and follow him in life and death.
265.35: A woman who commits sins against her husband alive or dead shall never get a husband in her re-birth. She will be the most unfortunate creature among women.
265.36: By not thinking of any one else and by serving her husband with devoted attention, a woman shall derive half the merit her husband achieves by the worship of God, propitiation of the manes and hospitality to guests.

267.1: O lord, for the bench t of everyone, please tell me, how, whether by making gifts or performing holy rites, can the ghosts be pleased.
267.2: O bird, please listen. I shall tell you about the gift which dispels all inauspicious obstacles.
267.3: What are the rites to be performed in his favour which can debar him from turning into a ghost?
267.4: Why are the five gems put unto the mouth of the dead? Why are gingelly seeds strewn on the ground? Why arc the Darbha blades scattered beneath?
267.5: Why do the sons and grandsons walk ahead? Why do they offer the gift of a lamp? Why do they adore Visnu?
267.6: Why do they, when ill, make a gift to a brahmin? Why do kinsmen, friends and enemies forgive them faults?
267.7: Why do they gift gingelly seeds, iron, gold, cotton, salt, seven types of grains, land or cow?
267.8: Why docs the son carry the corpse on his shoulders and the grandson light the fire? Why is the anointpient done with the butter?
267.9: Why are barley, mustard-seed, durva, stone and leaves of morgosa enjoined in the rite? Why do men 4nd women wear a lower and an upper garment?
267.10: Why should the meals be taken along with other persons on returning home? Why do the sons give nine pindas?
267.11: Why should the nine pindas be offered? How is the gift to be given to the gods and manes. Why is the call made for the bearers of the corpse? O lord, why is the rite of pinda repeated?
267.12: What should be given next after the gift of pina is made? Why are the bones collected? Why is a bed given to a brahmin in favour of the deceased?
267.13: Why should they anoint their bodies with oil. Why should the corpse-bearers be taken home on return from the cremation ground? Why should the corpse-bearers anoint their bodies with oil on the bank of a stream or a stagnant reservoir?
267.14: Why the sixteen sraddhas? Why are the food, water etc. given everyday for three hundred and sixty days of the year?
267.15: From where do the five thieves of the body—greed, affection, desire, love and pride go away, O lord!
267.16: Whatever little action has been done, whether good or bad, whatever gifts have been tendered which procure merit, where do these go away after the body has decayed?

268.1: O noble being, you have put pertinent questions to me. Listen to my explanation of all obsequial rites for the benefit of the people.
268.2: I shall explain the same on the authorities of the Vedas and Smrti texts. This has not been revealed even to gods and yogins who are devoted to meditation on the self.
268.3: The ground should be smeared with cow-dung. Gingelly seeds and Darbha grass should be strewn. The sick man put thereon will be able to burn off his sins.
268.4: Evil spirits, demons, ghosts and terrible giants of low strata attack the sick man lying on the ground which is not smeared with cowdung by the people.
268.5: If the daily homo, Srdddha or washing the feet of the holy brahmin guests arc performed on the bare ground without the mystic diagram drawn they arc no better than left undone.
268.6: Gingelly seeds originate from my sweat, O Garuda and hence are holy. Asuras, Danavas and Daityas flee from the place where gingelly seeds are kept.
268.7: Gingelly seeds, white, black or brown destroy sins committed by the body.
268.8: One gingelly seed offered in the holy rite is on a par with the gift of a drojaa measure of golden gingelly seeds.
268.9: Brahmins, mantras, kusa grass, fire and TulasI plant, O lord of birds, never become impure, though utilized fre¬ quently.
268.10: Kusas become impure, when used with pindas. Brahmins become impure when they partake ofpretafood. Mantras become futile when practised by Sudras. The fire in the funeral pyre is not so holy.
268.11: O bird, there are five types of boats to succour saintly men who may otherwise get drowned in the ocean of worldly existence— Tulasi, Brahmins, Cows, Visnu and the Ekadasi day.
268.12: In the worthless but impassable ocean of worldly existence there are six holy things yielding salvation— Viftiu, Ekadasi, Cahgd, Tulasi Brahmins and Cows.
268.13: Gingelly seeds are holy and unparalleled. Similarly, darbhas and Tulasi too. The three ward off mishaps.
268.14: Holding the Darbha grass in the hand, the performer of the rites shall sprinkle water over the ground. At the time of death, the darbha grass should be strewn near the bed of the dying person.
268.15: The dead body should be enveloped with darbha grass and placed over the bed made of the same grass. Then it is sure that the dead man will attain Vi9nu's region, even without the recital of mantras.

269.1: He who. makes a gift ofgingelly seeds, cow, plot of land or gold to a worthy brahmin will have his sins, accruing in different births, instantaneously quelled.
269.2: - The thiee mystical syllables prefixed to the Gayatri
269.3: Gingelly seeds and cows constitute the major gifts and they quell all major sins. The two should be given finly to a brahmin and never to a member of any other caste.
269.4: Gingelly seeds, cow, plot of land are given to brahmins after the rite of sankalpa. They are not given to the people of other castes. Sometimes, they are given to dependents also.
269.5: During the period of sickness, when the body is lying on the ground and during transport he will have no trouble.
269.6: Gingelly seeds, iron, gold, cotton, salt, seven grains, plot of land and cow—each constitutes a holy gift.
269.7: The gift of iron and gingelly seeds pleases Yama. The gift of salt wards off fear from Yama.
269.8: The gift of cotton wards off danger from the ghost. Cows gifted away enable the giver to cross all difficulties and save him from the threefold affliction®.
269.9: Threefold affliction: &dliyatmika—caused by the mind (sorrow, etc), udlndaivika—caused by fate (pain etc), adhibhautika—caused by living beings.
269.10: The emissaries of Yama who arc as terrific in appearance as Yama himself bestow boons if gifts of seven grains are made and they are satiated.
269.11: By remembering Visnu, one attains the highest goal. Thus, I have told you all about the goal attainable by the mortals.
269.12: If the son on seeing his father lying on the ground with the eyes half-closed makes gifts with the consent of his father, he is honoured by the gods.
269.13: The father being dead, the sons should perform the obsequial rites devotedly. Thus, they can make their father cross the ocean of distress.
269.14: What avail the abundance of charitable deeds. Enough that he performs the funeral rites of his father. Even the horse sacrifice does not merit a sixteenth part of the merit accruing from all these.
269.15: The son who makes gifts in favour of his father who is lying ill in death-bed is honoured even by the gods.
269.16: The father should make gifts of iron with his hands lixed in the ground. The giver of gifts never finds Yama terrific, lie will not go to his abode even.
269.17: Dagger, iron club, baton, sword and lancet are the weapons in the hands of Yama to curb sinners.
269.18: Hence, gifts of weapons shall be made. For, this gift is lor the propriation of Yama's weapons.
269.19: A child in the womb, infant in the arms, young men or old men can burn off their sins by means of these gifts.
269.20: The different emissaries of Yama—Ghurinas, an<as, Markas, Udumbarasare delighted by gifts of iron.
269.21: Sons, grandsons, kinsmen, clansmen, friends, wives, etc. of those who do not make such gifts are no better than the slayers of brahmins.
269.22: Listen to the course of a man dying on the earth. The first stage is that of Ativaha (the subtle body in transit); then that of ghost; then at the end of a year that of a pitr.
269.23: There are three fires, three worlds, three Vedas, three deities, three times, three junctures, three Varnas and three powers.
269.24: 1 am the vital air stationed inside the body of living beings. Considering the inclination of the living being as actuated by the actions of his previous birth, I mould the mind and divert it to virtue or evil, joy or sorrow, or things done or undone.
269.25: The prosperity of man, consigned to heaven or hell, is possible through Sraddhas. Hence, people shall assiduously perform different kinds of 3raddhas.
269.26: The names of the ten incarnations of the lord, viz— Matsya (fish), Kurma (tortoise), Varaha (boar), Narasiriiha, 3rirama, Parurama, Krna, Balarama, Buddha and Kalki shall be remembered always.
269.27: He will be posted in heaven. After enjoying the pleasures therein when he is born again on the £rth, he will enjoy riches. He will be endowed with the qualities of mercy and chivalry. He will have sons and grandsons. He will live for a hundred years.
269.28: He should offer gifts to the needy and adore Vi$nu
269.30: White flowers should be offered in worship together with food offerings cooked in ghee. Frequent incenses and scents should be offered and hymns from the Vedas, Smrtis such as of Manu should be recited.

269.32: I am gold. 1 am grains. I am honey. I am ghee. I am brahmins. I am deities. I am 8iva. I am mantras: bhuhy bhuvafyy svah.
269.33: 1 am the giver. I am the taker. 1 am the sacrificer. I am the sacrifice. I am the remover. I am virtue, earth and water.
269.34: O bird, I divert a man's mind to virtue or evil through auspicious and inauspicious activities. Whatever man does is actuated by the actions of his previous birth.

270.1: Men tainted by sins go to Yama's abode. A gift made in my name accords endless benefits.
270.2: A person who gifts plots of land stays in heaven for as many years as the number of steps the land measures. Those who make gifts of sandals go seated on horse-back.
270.3: By making a gift of umbrella one will traverse after death, without difficulty, the paths where other men are excessively oppressed by the heat of the sun.
270.4: Lamps shall be gifted daily for a year after the death for the benefit of the dead in the troublesome path.
270.5: He who makes gifts of a horse, a lx»at or an elephant to brahmins will become happy.
270.6: He who makes a gift of buffalo sojourns in many worlds. A she-buffalo, the mother of the vehicle of Yama, accords benefit.
270.7: A gift of betel leaves together with flowers increases the delight of those who are in Yama's abode. Being delighted with that they do not harass him.
270.8: If a person makes a gift of clothes, the awe-inspir¬ ing terrible emissaries of Yama black and tawny in colour do not threaten him.
270.9: By making gifts of potfuls of foodstuffs one shall be happy in those paths which one should otherwise have to traverse exhausted utterly and oppressed by thirst.
270.10: A bed with smooth cotton within and covered by a velvet cloth should be given to gods and brahmins. By that the dead man will be freed from ghosthood and rejoice with deities,
270.11: Thus, O Tarksya, I have explained to you the gifts which should be offered when performing obsequies. I shall now tell you how death enters the body.
270.12: It may escape through any of the nine apertures or through the pores of hair or through the palate. The subtle soul escapes through Ap&rud- in the case of sinners.
270.13: When the vital air escapes, the corpse falls down. When struck down by Death it falls like a tree bereft of its support.
270.14: The earthly matter becomes merged in the principle of fire. The gaseous matter becomes assimilated in the principle of wind. The ethereal matter gets dissolved in the principle of ether and the all-pervasive soul gets merged in Safikara.
270.15: The five vices—passion, etc. and the five sense- organs, O bird, are the villains stationed in the body.
270.16: Lust, anger and egotism are led by the mind which is the annihilating agent in collusion with merit and demerit.
270.17: Just as a householder enters a new furnished house after the former has been burnt and destroyed,.so also the soul enters a new body endowed with all objects and the five sense-organs.
270.18: All the bodies are invested with these attributes and features. All the deities and the fourteen worlds are present therein.
270.19: Those who do not understand themselves are no better than brutes. The four kinds of living beings have their bodies of the same nature and same content.
270.20: Eight million four hundred thousand varieties of creatures were created by me formerly.
270.21: They are svedajas (insects), Udbhijas, (plants), andajas (birds) and jarayujas, born from the womb, O sinless one, I have thus explained what you asked me.

271.1: Fourteen worlds —Roughly speaking there are three Ma5: heaven,
271.2: Four species: swdlaja-—generated by warm vapour or sweat (insects); udbhijja—sprouting, germinating (as a plant); aodaja—oviparous (birds) and jar&yuja—born from the womb, viviparous (human beings).
271.3: I shall tell you a great secret with the (fecisive method of unravelling the same, by knowing which one becomes omniscient.
271.4: O Garuda, you have put a pertinent question about the origin of life. Hence, listen attentively.
271.5: The first four days of menstrual flow of blood shall be avoided when the sin of a brahmin's slaughter resides in her.
271.6: Brahma had removed this sin from Indra' and apportioned a fourth in women. Hence, even the glancing at her face during these days shall be eschewed.
271.7: After seven days, she becomes pure enough to take part in the worship of manes and deities. If conception takes place within seven days the progeny is impure.
271.8: Whatever be the thoughts of parents during the intercourse, like that is the progeny. There is no doubt in this.
271.9: If the sexual intercourse takes place on even nights, boys are conceived and if on odd nights girls arc conceived. Hence, it is better to have sexual intercourse on even nights,- leaving the first seven days after the menstrual discharge.
271.10: Indra slew Vrtra and ihfrcby incurred the sin of BrahmahalyA Brahma removed the sin and apportioned the fourth part in the wonu n during the days of menstruation.
271.11: By sexual intercourse on odd nights, girls arc born, on even nights sons are born. MS III. 4.')-48
271.12: The semcn mixing with the blood causes the foetus. The foetus develops in the womb like the moon in the sky.
271.13: If the semen and the blood arc of equal potency, the child will be a eunuch. The nucleus of the foetus is formed within a day. It becomes frothy bubble in five days.
271.14: Within fourteen days it becomes a mixture of flesh and lymphatic substances.
271.15: It becomes a solid flesh in twenty days, sufficiently strong (in twenty five days) and (after that) it begins to develop gradually. The foetus would have assimilated complete¬ ly the five elements within a month.
271.16: By the time the two months are over, the fat and the skin are evolved. The marrow and the bones are*formed in three months time. The hair and the heels are formed in the fourth month.
271.17: The ears, nose and the belly are formed in the fifth month. The throat, back and the reproductive organs are developed in the seventh month.
271.18: By the eighth month, all the limbs are completed. In the beginning of the ninth month the child in the womb is fully developed.
271.19: Whether the child be a girl or a boy or a eunuch it comes out in the ninth or tenth month.
271.20: Then being dragged by the wind in the womb, agitated with pain, nourished by the susumna nerve in the woman's womb, the same comes out.
271.21: The saliva, urine, semen, marrow and blood constitute the parts predominant in the principle of water. They should be realized carefully.
271.22: Hunger, somnolence, thirst, lethargy and brilliance, O lord of birds, are considered by yogins as constituting the qualities of fire in the human constitution.
271.23: Love, hatred, bashfulness, fear and delusion are the qualities, O bird, derived from wind.
271.24: Running, breathing, contracting, stretching and thwarting are the qualities of wind in the physical body.
271.25: O bird, resonant sound, cavity, gravity, hearing and supporting everything are the qualities of Ethip'.
271.26: £arS} skin, eyes, tongue and nose are the five sense- organs. Hands, feet, rectum, phallus and speech are the hve organs of activity.
271.27: The ten vital airs stationed in the body are Prana, Apana, Samana, Udana, Vyana, Naga, Kurma, Krkara, Devadatta and Dhanafijaya.
271.28: The wind accords vitality and takes the assimilated food to all the joints of the body.
271.29: O son of Vinata, the roots of hair in the body are thirty five millions and the teeth are thirtytwo in number usually.
271.30: The nails are twenty and the hair growing on the face and head are seven hundred thousand. Generally, the fleshy matter in the body weighs about a thousand palas.
271.31: Pleasure, pain, fear and welfare—these come to a person by actions alone.
271.32: Thus the living being in the embryo of the mother develops gradually. The bones attain hardness. Life is sustained by food and drink.
271.33: In the womb he recollects the past events and happenings of worldly affairs. Tormented from all sides he feels depressed.
271.34: "As soon as I leave the womb I shall be very cautious. I shall never repeat mistakes. I shall so act that I may not be bom again."
271.35: The living being thinks thus and further recollects events of hundreds of past births—events which accrued to him from causes known and unknown.
271.36: Then at the scheduled time the living being emerges from the embryo with the head downward in the ninth or tenth month.
271.37: While leaving the womb he suffers and faints. When he comes out of the womb he cries in anguish.
271.38: In childhood he remains in that state; passing through childhood he attains youth and old age.
271.39: Then he succumbs to death, then he attains birth. Thus, on the wheel of existence he is made to rotate like the potter's wheel.
271.40: Sometimes he goes to heaven, sometimes to hell. In heaven or hell he reaps the fruits of his activities.
271.41: Sometimes, when he has exhausted the merit of his actions he descends to the earth by the residue of his merits. Heaven or hell is not a permanent abode, this you should know, O best of birds.
271.42: People going to hell suffer from extreme tortures which they derive from their hellish activities. Their tortures increase when they see their companions enjoying in heaven.
271.43: Extreme distress awaits the inmates even in the celestial region inasmuch as the thought of fear haunts their mind from the very start they enter heaven that after their merits are exhausted they would be thrown into hell.
271.44: Looking at the tortures suffered by the people in hell, the residents of heaven feel that after the expiry of their merit the same fate awaits them in hell. Thus all the while they remain discomfortable in heaven.
271.45: In youth he suffers from the evil effects of vicious desires, jealousy, rage. He is afflicted by bad dreams. Old age ends in death which is extremely painful.
271.46: Being dragged by the emissaries of Yama he is thrust into hell. From hell he descends to the earth to suffer again the utmost pangs of birth and death.
271.47: Thus, on the wheel of this universe, people are made to rotate like the potter's wheel and are tortured incessantly, tangled by the noose of their actions.
271.48: Thus, I have told you all about the child in the womb. I now answer your further query in the serial order, if you desire to hear.
271.49: I am satiated with the answer to both of my queries. I implore you, now, to answer my third query too.
271.50: You have asked me what should be done for a dying person. Now listen, I shall tell you my answer in brief to your query.
271.51: His head should be put in the east or in the north with gold in the mouth.
271.52: O lord of birds, Salagram stone and TulasI leaves should be kept nearby. An earthen lamp should be kindled. He should utter: Orh namo bhagavate V&sudevdya.
271.53: He should draw Om at first, worship the same and offer charity.
271.54: He should worship lord Visnu with flowers, incense etc, and pay homage glorifying his deeds and concentrating on him with sincere devotion. He should offer charity to the brahmins, poor and the indigent.
271.55: He should give up attachment for the son, friend, wife, fields, corns, wealth and set his heart on Visnu.
271.56: I have told you all that can be done when death is imminent. Now, 1 shall tell you, in brief, the fruits of all these activities.
271.57: Bath purifies a man, removes impurity. Meditation on Vi?nu yields all sorts of fruits.
271.58: A blade of darbha grass takes him to heaven. There
271.59: A circle should be drawn around the dying person, for, it is said, Brahma, Visnu, Rudra, Laksmi and hre reside within the circle.
271.60: By muttering the mantra Orii namo bhagavaU Vasudivaya, one is completely absorbed in Brahma. Even by worshipping me alone, one can reach my region direct.
271.61: In the obsence of entanglement, attachment vanishes by the knowledge as revealed in the Purufa Sukta.
271.62: Seven lower regions descending from the earth one below the other arc named Atola, Vitala, Satala, Taldtala, Rasdtala, Mahdtala and Pdtdla while seven higher regions rising from the earth one above the other are called Bhur, Bhuvar Svar, Mahar, Janas, Tapar, Satya or Brahma.
271.63: They live in the region of Yama and when they are reborn they will be born in cottages. O Tarkya, thus, man is born in the mortal world as a result of his own actions.
271.64: Happiness or misery, fear or welfare are the results of actions. The foetus lies in the womb with the feet up and the face downwards.
271.65: From the moment of birth the Maya of Vi§nu enamours and deludes the life. The life takes its birth with its association brought about by its own actions.
271.66: Due to merit, man enjoys pleasures in heaven and is fortunalety born in a noble family*. If he is sinful in actions he is born in a mean-minded family.
271.67: He becomes poor, sick, foolish, sinful and miserable. O son of a sage, I have thus told you the various features of the birth of a life.

272.1: O lord, what are the merits or demerits, sins or virtues, as a result of which men go there. Please tell me all -concerning this.
272.2: The distance between the mortal world and the region of Yama is eighty six thousand yojanas (one million thirty two thousand kilometres).
272.3: There are many sharp thorns of awful appearance. The area is entirely covered by the burning fire.
272.4: Many arc oppressed by hunger and many by thirst on that High path. On that impassable path of Yama many shiver with chillness.
272.5: The wayfarers find the path difficult in accordance with the gravity of their sins. They are helpless, miserable and confounded as they plod on.
272.6: Some bemoan piteously, some speak harshly. Agitat¬ ed by the effects of their actions they undergo endless distress.
272.7: O bird, that pathway has some special characteristics. Those who have been devoid of convetousness in the world procceed along that path peacefully.
272.8: The various gifts that people make in the world stand them in good stead in the region of Yama. They go- ahead (and make everything comfortable).
272.9: Sraddhas and water libations are of no avail to the sinner. These wretches hover here and there in their aerial form,
272.10: O good one who are devoted to virtue, the pathway has been narrated to you thus. Now I shall tell you the hard¬ ships one has to undergo on the way to the region of Yama.
272.11: The city extends over a thousand Yojanas (1200 km.) and is studded with gems resplendent like lightning, blazing fire and the sunshine.
272.12: The special palace of Yama with its golden splendour is very extensive and twentyfive yojanas in height.
272.13: The wind blows there very gently. Many festivals are celebrated there. Many sages conduct discourses there. Different musical instruments are played.
272.14: There, seated in his wonderful driving seat he calculates the age of human beings and others.
272.15: To the north of the central seat, the abode of Cholera can be seen. To the north-east the abode of Head-ache and to the south-east the abode of Unconsciousness.
272.16: Dysentery resides in the south-west and the Burning sensation in the north-west. Citragupta is ever surrounded by these. Whatever job is executed by them is immediately written down by Citragupta.
272.17: O Tark§ya, the messengers stay in different places at the threshhold of the palace of Dharmaraja torturing the sin¬ ful wretches of evil human beings.
272.18: Men are bound with nooses by the messengers of Yama and thrashed with heavy iron clubs. All that is in accordance with their own evil actions.
272.19: They are hit and beaten with various weapons and different mechanical devices. They are split with saws and scissors as though they were pieces of lumber.
272.20: Others are seen being dragged here and there on the ground and chopped with sharp knives. They are seen wailing and shouting. All this is due to their own evil actions.

274.2: Three generations from one are those who share the pinda. The next three generations are those who do not share the pinda. The next three generations are those who receive the wipings of the food-offerings sticking to the hand and the tenth is near the line.
274.3: These are the names assigned to men in one's father's as well as mother's family. The householder who performs the sraddhas saves ten preceding and ten succeeding generations.
274.4: Grandfather of the fourth degree of the first tyajaka is the first lepaka [i.e. the 7th grandfather reckoning from the householder]. Grandfatlier of the 4th degree of the first lepaka is in the 10th degree since he is the fourth in reckoning from the 7 th one.
274.5: Now, listen to the benefit accruing from performing the sraddhas and offering gifts according to astras in favour of the dead.
274.6: The father blesses the performer with the birth of sons, the grandfather with cattle-wealth and the great-grand- iather with coins of gold.
274.7: Such are the benefits derivable from sraddhas and tarpanas. The great grandfather blesses one with plenty of foodstuffs.
274.8: Or he may be born in other species of living beings such as a tree, a bird, a reptile. If a child is born and dies, the man cannot be freed from hell, still.
274.9: For his sake the Netr&yana bali should be performed by his preceptor or disciple or even by a distant relative.
274.10: He will be freed from sins and saved from hell. He will stay permanently in heaven. No doubt need be entertained on this account.

274.12: Four effigies of Darbha are consecrated with the mantras of the naksatras. These are thrown beside the corpse.
274.13: The man who dies on any of these five days does not attain salvation unless for his sake the gingelly seeds, cow, gold and ghee arc gifted away.
274.14: Gifts are made to brahmins to ward off impending calamity after the expiry of impurity period. QTts help the deceased attain release from the bonds of his previons actions.
274.15: O bird, a third method of reckoning the sixteen Sraddhas is as follows:— the twelve monthly Sraddhas together with that on the eleventh, that on tripaksa (after the expiry of si.x weeks) and those on the two rikta days.
274.16: The first set of sixteen Sraddhas are for purifying the corpse. The fifty Sriddhas are for purifying the line of Manes (pitrpankti).
274.17: Ceremonial ablutions, gifts, sacrifices, water- libations and worship of gods are futile when performed with a dead body in the village. The convention holds good for all kiths and kins.
274.18: O lord of birds, this convention prevails among cousins and kins. If it is violated, the dead man is tarnished by sins.

275.1: If any one observes the rite of fasting and dies he will cast off his human form and become equal in lustre to me.
275.2: He will have the benefit of performing as many sacrifices, complete with due fees as the number of days he was able to live observing the rite of fasting.
275.3: If such a death takes place after taking to Sannyasa whether in the holy centre or elsewhere the benefit accruing from the same is twice that of the previous one.
275.4: If a person suffering from an incurable disease such as plague etc. observes fast and dies he has no rebirth. He rejoices in heaven like a deity.
275.5: Brahmins should be fed everyday. Gifts of a vessel full of gingelly seeds or gifts of lamps according to his capacity should be made. Gods should also be worshipped.
275.6: If gifts are made in favour of the dead, his major and minor sins are washed away. On death, he attains immor¬ tality on par with sages.
275.7: Hence, observance of fast enables men to attain heaven. Man should strive for salvation when his body is in perfect health.
275.8: The deities Brahma and others bestow contentment and nourishment on the man who forsakes his sons, wealth and goes to a holy centre.
275.9: If a person dies after observing the fast on reaching the holy centre or on the way, he goes to the sphere of sages.
275.10: If a person dies at home after observing the fast he alone will sojourn in heaven leaving the members of his family.
275.11: If a person casts off food and water and drinks only the water from my feet he is not reborn on the earth.
275.12: The family deities protect the man who goes to a holy centre and abstains from food. The emissaries of Yama guard him. No torture at the hands of Yama's attendants is in store for him.
275.13: A person who makes frequent pilgrimages to holy centres can destroy sins. The person who cremates him, if he dies, enjoys the benefit of making the pilgrimage.
275.14: A frequent visitor to holy centres, even if he dies outside the holy centre, is reborn as an intelligent Brahmin well-versed in the Vedas at a holy place and in a noble family.
275.15: If a man observing fast, O Tarksya, survives it he should invite brahmanas and gift away his possessions.
275.16: Following the instructions of brahmins he should observe Candrayana and Krcchra. He should never tell a lie thereafter. He shall practise virtuous actions.
275.17: When a person returns to his own house after making pilgrimage to the holy centre he should take the permission of pious brahmins and perform expiatory rites.
275.18: A person starting on a pilgrimage when death is imminent should make gifts of cows at every step if the act is not involved in violence.
275.19: Even indigent persons when sick shmild make gifts. Such gifts should consist of a cow, gingelly seeds, gold and of seven gins*
275.20: On seeing a person making liberal gifts, the deities, sages and Citragupta are excessively delighted.
275.21: By offering gifts of wealth to brahmapas, the sons in fact, prepare for their salvation along with sons, grandsons and great grandsons.
275.22: If, out of covetousness, a person does not give any thing during sickness, that miserly sinner will indeed repent after death.
275.23: Just as an unchaste wife laughs at her husband who fondles the son too much, as also death laughs at a person who makes fuss about protecting himself, and the earth laughs at a person who guards too much his wealth.
275.24: The after-effects of death in water last for seven thousand years; thcae of death in fire for eleven thousand years; those of death in scorching sun for sixteen thousand years; those of death in a battle for sixty thousand years; those of death in thwarting the seizure of cow for eighty thousand years, and O Bharata, those of death in fasting are everlasting.

276.1: O Tarksya, now I shall explain the mode of gifting a water-jar. It should be offered to the brahman in favour of the dead along with a rice-ball and the libation of water.
276.2: For the pleasure of the dead on their way to Yama's abode, these vessels should be given on the twelfth day, after six weeks, after six months or at the end of a year.
276.3: The vessel should be placed on the ground cleaned and smeared with cowdung. They should be filled with cooked food and water.
276.4: Satiating food should be given to the dead. The dead man is delighted thereby as he goes along with the attendants of Yama.
276.5: On the twelfth day, twelve such jars should be given.
276.6: A Vardhani [a vessel] filled with cooked food and water should be given to a brahmin with Visnu in view after due sathkalpa.
276.7: Sixteen vessels filled with cooked black gram and water should be given to sixteen brahmanas, one to each.
276.8: The sixteen <$raddhas are performed beginning with Utkranti-raddha (the first of the scries).
276.9: From the eleventh day a vessel should be given every day for a year.
276.10: A Vardhani filled with cooked rice and water should be given everyday for a year along with a bamboo vessel.
276.11: A vessel full of water should be gpven to a brahmin, after covering it with a cloth and scenting it with fragrant stuffs.

277.1: After obtaining human form in any of the thirteen castes in Bharata, if a man dies in a holy centre he is never born again.
277.2: The seven cities of Ayodhya, Mathura, Maya, Kaflci,. Avantika, Kaii and Dvaravati confer salvation.
277.3: If at the time when the vital airs have reached the throat (when death is imminent) a man says T have renounc¬ ed*, he attains the region of Visnu after death and is not bom again.
277.4: He has already tucked his clothes for his journey to his goal of salvation if he pronounces the two letters Hari even for once.
277.5: He who remembers me ever and anon saying krftfa, krfi?a is lifted up by me from hell just as the lotus springs up breaking through the water.
277.6: Undoubtedly one attains salvation if one dies near a Salagrama stone which is powerful for annihilating all sins and defects.
277.7: O bird, by growing, nurturing, sprinkling, saluting and extolling the TulasI plant Man's sin accumulated in various births is wiped off.
277.8: He who has taken ablution in the holy lake of Manasa where wisdom is the eddy, truth the water and which removes the dirt of love and hatred is never tarnished by sins.
277.9: Fishermen visit Narmada, the holy river, every morning. But their mind does not become pure.
277.10: Men reap the fruits of their actions in accordance with their feeling; their goal in the other world is also befitting that. Their activity yields accordant fruits.
277.11: He who lays down his life for the sake of his preceptor, a brahmin a woman or a child attains salvations.
277.12: After making various gifts to brahmins if a person dies during the period of fast he is freed from all bondage and attains salvation.
277.13: Casting themselves off, human beings whether of high, middling or low class attain their heavenly abode.

277.15: He who offers a virgin in marriage to a brahmin well versed in the Vedas shall stay in Indraloka along with the members of his family.
277.16: If a woman leaves her sons, grandsons and other relatives and follows her husband in death both of them attain heaven along with three generations.
277.17: Even if a woman has committed sins including evil intention against her own husband she can wash off her sins if she follows her husband in death.
277.18: Even if the husband has been a sinner and wicked, his sins will be washed off if the wife follows him after death.
277.19: If a man offers only a morsel of bread to the needy he will be proceeding to heaven in an aerial chariot endowed with chowries and umbrellas.
277.20: If he offers maintenance sufficient for a year, the sins committed by him till his death are destroyed.
277.21: If he helps a brahmin to celebrate the marriage of his daughter, he washes off his sins of the past, future and present births.

278.1: O lord, out of compassion for me, please tell me the rules of impurity, for my knowledge and for the welfare of human beings.
278.2: O lord of birds, the impurity accruing from birth and death is fourfold. The rules of impurity are applicable to all the four castes.
278.3: The days of impurity are ten for the relatives on the father*s and mother's side. People should avoid taking meals, during this period, with the relatives of the dead. The bereaved fiunily should neither offer nor receive gifts, should neither undertake nor conduct sacrifices. The study of the Vedas and ifistras is stricdy prohibited.
278.4: One should observe the following while performing obsequial rites: suitability of place and time, sufficiency of wealth, justiffcation of purpose, validity of reason and his capability.
278.5: Artisans, architects, physicians, slaves (male or female), kings and Vedic scholars are purified immediately.
278.6: In impurity accruing from birth, the rules are less strict. Mother is purified after ten days, father just after taking bath.
278.7: During the days of marriage, festivity, sacrifice, if a person dies, there is no impurity. The food-stuff collected for use can be utilized by the persons concerned. This is what Manu hzis said.
278.8: In birth the relatives incur no impurity. Impurity attaches to parents alone. Primarily, it is the mother who be¬ comes impure. Father is purified by the touch of water alone.
278.9: In birth or death impurity lasts for ten days, O bird.
278.10: By giving food to the hungry and the indigent, the parents get rid of impurity—the sages have declared.
278.11: A person distanced by seven or eight generation or he who has not undergone a Sacrament incurs no impurity.
278.12: For men who have lost life for the sake of a brahmin, a cow, a woman or in the battlefield, infirmity lasts only for a single night.
278.13: When udras, following a corpse, reach a pond or a stream or a reservoir, they should return home. While return¬ ing they should be glanced at by a brahmin which is enough for their purification. This is what the Vedic scholars say.

279.1: O Garu<iia, I shall tell you in detail about their passage, rules of observance and place. It is a great secret— the rite in case of abnormal death.
279.2: For a brahmin, the rite should be performed within six months; for a ksatriya within three months; for a vaiiya within a month and a half and for a iudra immediately.
279.3: Rites accompanied by reciting the Purusa-sukta and Visnu mantras should be performed. Facing the south, the dead should be identified with lord Visnu.
279.4: The mantra runs thus! "May the lord Punarikaksa who has no beginning, no end, who bears on his person a conch, a discus and a mace confer salvation to the dead.
279.5: Then he shall perform eleven sraddhas with full concentration observing all rules.
279.6: Gifts should be made to all without depriving any¬ one of the line of those assembled. The rice-balls placed on the ground should be accompanied by scents, flowers and grains.
279.7: Gifts made to brahmins should be in accordance with the Vedic and Gastric injunctions. Water-libation should be offered separately through a conch or a copper vessel.
279.8: The performer of rites should hold breath and kneel on the ground. He should first give the arghya and then per¬ form ekoddista.
279.9: The first rice-ball should be offered with the mantras dpo daivP madhumati and the second with the mantra Upay&magrhitosP.
279.21: Five brahmins should be invited and arghya given to them. They should be learned, of good conduct, most excellent in their family, free from physical decrepitude and noble. Never should they be of the condemnable type.
279.22: The image of Visnu should be made of gold, that of Rudra of copper, that of Brahma of silver and that ofYama of iron.
279.23: The effigy of the dead should be made of lead or Darbha grass. Nyasa of Samavedin should be conducted with the mantra Tam&ya tvd.
279.24: In five vessels containing five gems there be invoked Brahma, Visnu, Rudra, Yama and the dead person.
279.25: The cloth, the sacred thread and the coins should be separate for each deity. The mantras too are separate for each deity.
279.26: Five sraddhas are performed separately for the deities with due observance of rules, and water is poured over the pindas separately.
279.30: An effigy should be made with the medicinarherbs. O Kayapa, Palaia leaves and bunches should be split into several pieces.
279.31: The hide of a black deer should be spread and the effigy of kuia grass placed over it. Three hundred and sixty blades ofkusa grass representing the number of bones in the body should be used.
279.32: The blades ofkusa grass should be tied well to constitute the different limbs. Forty blades ofkusa grass at the head and ten at the neck.
279.33: Twenty in the region of the heart, twenty in the belly, hundred in the thighs and twenty at the hips.
279.34: Four for the penis, six for the testicles, ten for the toes. This is the procedure to represent the bones.
279.35: Sulphur represents the Dhatus (the principal constituents of the body). Haritala', Manahsila and fried barley flour represent flesh and honey represents the blood.
279.36: A clump of twigs and leaves represents the matted hair, hide of deer represents the skin, mercury represents semen and brass pieces the faeces.
279.37: Lotus petals are placed on the nose and the um¬ bilical region; brinjal on the testicles and red garlic on the penis.
279.38: Ghi should be applied over the navel. Lac represents the loin cloth. Pearls are placed at the breast and saffron over the head.

281.1: As a calf can trace its mother cow among a thousand cows, so also the actions done in previous births can follow the doer.
281.2: The sun, Vanina, Vi?nu, Brahma, moon, fire and lord Siva appreciate the person who gifts plots of land.
281.3: Even persons committing heinous sins are purified merely by making gift of a cow or a plot of land.
281.4: If someone seizes cows or land unlawfully due to greed he should be stopped. He goes to hell who does not protect these.
281.5: Even when the vital airs stick to the throat (when death is imminent) actions unworthy of performance should not be carried out; only worthy actions should be followed. This is known to Vedic scholars who have declared thus.
281.6: If a person voluntarily gifts something and wontonly seizes the same he becomes a great sinner. He goes to hell where he stays till the universe is dissolved in Deluge.
281.7: The merit that accrues to one in offering protection to a poor brahmin who is emaciated due to unemployment cannot be surpassed in sacredness even by performing a horse sacrifice accompanied by all sacrificial fees.
281.8: The merit one secures by guarding the Vedas and performing sacrifices accompanied by sacrificial gifts cannot equal the merit of protecting a weak brahmin.
281.9: The Vehicles and forces maintained with the wealth misappropriated from the brahmins break down at the time of battle like bunds made of sand.
281.10: The brahmanical asset enjoyed by the deception of affection burns the entire family till the seventh generation. The same if enjoyed stealthily burns the race so long as the moon and the. stars shine in the sky.
281.11: Clever persons may be there who can digest powder¬ ed iron or stone or even poison. But is there a man in the world who can digest the property of a brahmin?
281.12: By destroying the wealth of gods (temples), by seizing a brahmin's wealth or by dishonouring and slighting a brahmin a family falls in esteem.
281.13: Gifts made during the transit of the sun from one sign of Zodiac to the other, Havyas and Kavyas offered at that time enable one to be honoured in heaven for seven Kalpas.
281.14: Out of the three—acceptance of monetary gifts, imparting knowledge to the seeker and presiding over another man's sacrifice, acceptance of monetary gifts is the best. The sin, if any, in the acceptance of monetary gifts is removed by japas and homas but even the Vedas do not sanctify a person who presides over another man's sacrifice but himself does not perform any sacrifice.

282.2: Either the mother or a kinsman can perform the expiatory rite on behalf of a boy less than twelve but above four.
282.3: Boys of less than four years in age can never be guilty or sinful. Even the king cannot punish them. There is no expiatory rite prescribed for such boys, in the iastras.

283.3: Then again, he should worship lord Visnu and Yama with sandal paste, flowers, incense, lamp and eatables.
283.4: He should keep fast on that day and invite the brahmanas of noble families, of good character, learned and austere.
283.5: They may be nine or seven or five, according to his ability. Next day, at noon, Visnu and Yama should be worshipped.
283.6: The brahmins should be seated facing the north. Lord V4pu and Yama should be invoked and worshipped.
283.7: The performer of the rite should keep wearing the sacred thread to the right. He should name the dea4 and think upon him, lord Vinu and Yama and complete the rite.
283.8: He should remember his other ancestors too and offer pinda to each separately or all together. Ten or five pindas, as prescribed, should be offered.
283.9: First, he should offer a pind to Vijiiu, then to Brahma, Siva, his attendents and then the fifth to the dead.
283.10: While offering a pina he should utter the name and surname of the dead and the name of lord VisOu. Bowing with head, he should give the fifth pind to the departed soul.
283.11: Remembering the dead he should give, according to his ability, a cow, a plot of land, articles of food, gingclly seeds to the brahmanas with darbha grass in hand.
283.12: So also coins, betel and corn should be given to the brahmanas. The headman among the brahmanas should be honoured with gold.
283.13: Taking the personal name and the surname of the dead the performer should gift the articles with the formula: May Visnu be pleased. While the brahmanas are leaving he should follow them with his face to the south and throw water over the earth.
283.14: While he throws water over the earth, he should mention the name and surname of the dead and pronounce: 'May the departed soul be pleased'. 284.1: O Foremost among birds, I shall now tell you the mode of annual raddha. Either the ksetraja or the aurasa -son should perform the annual Iraddha in the manner as he performs the parvana Sraddha.
284.2: If at the time of pihva jr&ddha the performer is defiled by impurity he should perform it on the expiry of impurity.
284.3: The iraddha of a ludra should be performed silently {i.c. without reciting mantras) by his wives or sons. The same holds good in the case of a iraddha of an unmarried girl in a brahmin family. So says Manu.
284.4: If two or more die at the same time, the bathing shall be done simultaneously with due mantras but raddhas should be performed separately.
284.5: The iraddha of the eldest should be performed first and thereafter according to the age. This is the procedure in simultaneous deaths.
284.6: He who docs all this every year without fail will obtain the best of state having liberated all the manes.
284.7: If both the day and the month of death are not known then the day and the month when he set out on journey - should be taken into count for sraddha as stated by me before.
284.8: Even if the day and the month of starting are not known then those should be the same when the news of his death is received.
284.9: Even if the month and day are forgotten, when he is not on travel, these should be taken as before.
284.10: The Iraddha that has been started by the sons should be finished by them while the householder shall remain aloof.
284.11: If a donor or a receiver does not know of impurity due to birth or death of a relative then no fault accrues.
284.12: If either of these knows impurity accruing from death or birth of a relative, the fault is of the receiver only, not of the donor of the gift.
284.13: Whosoever performs the death anniversary of the dead in the above way, liberates him even if the day of death remains unknown to him.
284.14: In the daily Iraddha the brahmins shall be worshipp¬ ed, according to one's capacity, with scents and other things and the manes should be invoked and worshipped.
284.15: With the Visvedevas in view, the brahmins are fed sumptuously. This rite of feeding the brahmins is called Nitya raddha or Deva sraddha.
284.16: In the sraddha to the mother, if brahmins are not available, eight noble and chaste ladies whose husbands and sons are alive should be fed.
284.17: The person performing nitya, daiva and vfddha iraddhas as well as the kamya and naimittika rites in the manner as mentioned before achieves the desired result.

285.1: The different kinds of heavenly enjoyments, worldly pleasures, strength, nourishment and valour men acquire by the power of merit.
285.2: All these happen to meritorious persons here or there, it is true, definitely true. The lord's statement cannot be otherwise.
285.3: Virtue triumphs, not evil. Truth triumphs not false- hood. Forgiveness wins, not anger. Vi$nu conquers not the asuras.
285.4: I have understood this truth that everything auspi¬ cious results from merit. When our merit is at the peak we are devoted to lord Krta.
285.5: O Tkhya, men indulge in activities which result in meritorious or inauspicious fruits. O Kaiyapa, now listen how men derive traits from their particular activities.
285.6: The preceptor guides the seeker, the king chastens the wicked, Yama regulates and rectifies the person of secret sins.
285.7: Having suffered and crossed tortures in hell they return to the world of mortals marked with the characteristic signs.
285.8: If a person has been guilty of falsehood in speech, he becomes a stammerer, a teller of lies or dumb. The brahmin slayer is bom consumptive or leprous; the wine>addict becomes black-toothed.
285.9: The thief of gold becomes bad-nailed; the defiler of the preceptor's bed becomes ugly-skinned; he who associates with sinners is bom in a low family.
285.10: He who takes meals at another's house without prior invitation is born a crow. A brahmin who performs a sacrifice for low castes is born a village-pig. He who performs many such sacrifices is born an ass.
285.11: He who eats unscrupulously becomes a tiger in wilderness. He who scolds others without a cause becomes a cat; he who burns dry wood is born a glow-worm.
285.12: He who imparts knowledge to the undeserving' be¬ comes a bull. He who offers stale food to a brahmin becomes a hunch-back. He who is malicious to others is born blind. He who steals a book is bom similarly.
285.13: He who sells the forbidden articles becomes deform¬ ed in the eye. He who censures others is born of defiled womb. He who deceives a woman becomes an owl.
285.15: The seller of forbidden fruits becomes indigent. He who keeps a i§udra woman as concubine becomes a bull. He who kicks the sacred fire becomes a cat. He who eats another's meat becomes a patient.
285.16: He who indulges in sex at the prohibited time becomes a eunuch. A stealer of scents becomes a foul-smeller. A stealer of other goods becomes a swallow.
285.17: O lord of birds, these and other signs brought about by their actions are seen in men and others.
285.18: Persons who commit such sins fall into hell and are re-born in different species of animals.
285.19: After passing through these births men and women are re-born in human form when their merit and demerit are equalized.
285.20: When men and women unite in sexual act and both the semen and the blood are mixed, the child born will be nourished with all the elements in proper proportion.

286.1: O lord of gods, please tell me the mode of gifts, their glory and greatness and the magnitude of Vaitarani.
286.2: Listen to the magnitude of the dreadful Vaitarani, the mighty river at the threshold of Yama's city.
286.3: There blaze as many as twelve suns as it were the time of Deluge. The sinful people groan aloud and fall into it.
286.4: "Alas brother, alas son, alas mother'*, they shout frequently. They try to swim about but sink in it.
286.5: Those who have slighted their mothers, preceptors or priests can stay there permanently.
286.6: So also those who forsake their chaste, virtuous and noble wives without any fault.
286.7: Those who deceive their credulous masters, friends and sages, women, children, cripples and others get submerged in the putrid slough and groan there painfully.*

286.13: As a result of his noble actions one obtains pleasure here and hereafter. Its efficacy is increased a thousandfold if a healthy man makes this gift. If a sick man makes the gift its efficacy is only a hundredfold.

286.15: O sages, these details on the origin of creatures which I have mentioned to you arc conducive to salvation, as also the rites of obsequies. I shall now mention the great panacea for the removal of ills and sufferings of this mortal world.

287.1: The people of all castes who live in this mortal world die at their own time and obtain different worlds according to the magnitude of their pious deeds.
287.2: They go on different paths ordained by God. Through what virtue they obtain pleasure and through what merit they get family, strength and age? Tell me O lord.
287.3: On hearing this, the lord said to Garuda, explaining in detail how the body functions, how it is boimd by actions.
287.4: The ksatriya who has drunk blood from his forehead in the battle, has as well drunk Soma in the sacrifice; dead or alive he gets release.
287.5: Though he may have done many impious acts and drunk many undesirable drinks, if he takes weapons and faces the enemy in the war he is released from sins immediately,
287.6: Due to policy or fear, if a person does not face the foe in war, O bird, know it for certain that he is sure to die one day afterwards but before that his katrahood goes in vain. If he donates gold or earth to a brahmaa, he is born in human form in this world in a noble and illustrious fomily.

287.11: Whatever religious acts they have done keeping them in view and moving in the way, hear O bird, what they speak about among themselves.
287.12: The three in the world are the best of all: Jambu- dvipa among the dvipas, the land of the bright among the countries of the world and human beings amongst all creatures on the earth.
287.13: There are four castes—brahmin, katriya, vaisya and ludra. Among these the brahmin caste is the best. People can derive pleasure from religion. When they start on the High way, leaving their bodies after death, they revive their previous associations.
