288.1: O ocean of mercy! I have heard that this world of creatures is born out of ignorance. Now, I wish to hear the infallible method of Final Release.
288.2: O God, O deity of deities, O lover of refugees in this insignificant world filled with the filth of sorrows!
288.3: There are creatures staying in many bodies, being born and dying. There is no end to this process.
288.4: Hear, O bird, I shall tell you what you ask about Simply by hearing the same, you will get release from the world of mortals.
288.5: The creatures are his parts and parcels. Like sparks of fire being struck by the beginningless knowledge, they separate into different bodies, through beginninglcss actions.
288.6: They are controlled by virtues and vices in the form of bliss and sorrow. Their bodies have different castes, age and enjoyment born of their different actions.
288.7: Then again in every birth, O bird, they obtain subtle bodies and after attaining mokfa they acquire indestruc¬ tible frames.
288.8: The departed souls enter into insentient objects, worms, birds, animals, men, deities but after release do not enter into any object or any body at all.
288.9: Passing through four types of bodies in order of their karman and leaving one body after the other a thousand times, taking birth in human form and acquiring knowledge due to good acts one obtains release.
288.10: In the eightyfour lacs of bodies of creatures one does not acquire true knowledge anywhere unless one is born as man.
288.11: Here, after thousands of crores of births a creature obtains human form only sometime due to the aggregate of virtue.
288.12: Having obtained a rare human form he should endeavour for moka. If he does not endeavour for it, there can be no greater sinner in the world.
288.13: Born in the most beautiful human form he incurs the sin of slaying a brahmin if he neglects his self.
288.14: If alive, he may reap the result of his good actions. He may get a village, a field, a house or a wealth. But he may not get human body again.
288.15: A wise man finds out means to preserve his body. Even a leper does not wish to discard it.
288.16: If a person cannot protect himself from evil then who else will do the same?
288.17: If he cannot treat the disease here itself how shall he cure himself hereafter, at a place where' there is no medicine?
288.18: So far as sorrow does not come, calamities do not approach, organs do not defunct, one should practice virtue.
288.19: So far as this body remains intact he should practice virtue. One is a perfect fool who digs a well only when the house is on fire.
288.20: Even after seeing the distressed, the dead, the fallen and the aggrieved people do not ever fear having drunk the wine of infatuation.
288.21: When the soul comes and stays in the body like the foam of water, when the company of the beloved is but temporary, how can a person stay fearless?
288.22: He who does not know reality calls as useful what is useless, as permanent what is impermanent and as meaningful what is meaningless.
288.23: Being infatuated by divine illusion he falters even seeing, misunderstands even hearing and misses sense even readily.
288.24: Even when the crocodiles in the form of death, disease, old age are drowning this world in the ocean of time, he does not realize the Truth.
288.25: It may be possible to wrap the wind, rend the ether, knot the waves but it is not possible to maintain perpetuity of the age.
288.26: I have a son, wife, wealth and relations. Thus, while the goat of man thinks, the wolf of time takes him away by force.
288.27: Split with the needle of greed, soaked in_thc oil of passions, cooked in the fire of anger and envy, man is eaten up by death.
288.28: Death takes away even children, young people, old men and those in womb—such is this world.
288.29: Not to speak of wife, mother, father, son and other relatives, the soul leaves even his own body and goes to the abode of Yama.
288.30: This world has sorrow as the root. Whosoever possesses the same is sorrowful. Whosoever leaves it is happy.
288.31: Man can get rid of fetters of iron and wood but not the fetters in the form of his son and wife.
288.32: So far as a being makes relations deaf to heart, the cones of sorrow are being pegged in his heart.
288.33: Just as the fish tempted by flesh does not see the iron-cone, so also a creature, tempted by enjoyment does not anticipate Yama's torture.
288.34: The people going on the wrong path do not dis¬ tinguish between good and evil. These men deserve hell, O bird, who are engaged only in filling up their bellies.
288.35: Sleep, fear, sex and food are equal for all creatures. He who possesses knowledge is a man and he who is without knowledge is an animal.
288.36: Foolish people are troubled by natural call in the morning, by hunger and thirst at midday and by sex and sleep at night.
288.37: People love their bodies, wealth, wives, etc. Alas! being infatuated by ignorance they are born and they die.
288.38: Therefore, one should always shun company. If it is not possible, one should associate with the great.
288.39: Association with the good and discrimination are two clear eyes. Whosoever lacks them is a blind man who can go astray from the right path.
288.40: Men are busy with their own affairs devolved on them by their ancestral profession or by their paticular stage in life. They do not know about true religion. Being deceitful they perish.
288.41: Why should many preachers practising vows, but with their vision blinded by ignorance laboriously move here and there.
288.42: Can the ignorant fools get release by torturing their body? Can a serpent die simply by beating the hole wherein it dwells?
288.43: The imposters who guise themselves wjth matted hair and deer-skins and pretend to be pious move about deceiving people.
288.44: For him who takes delight in the pleasures of the world and pretends that he knows Brahman, both Karman and Brahman are far distant.
288.45: Alike at home and in forest, naked and shameless, the donkeys move here and there. Do they become unattached?
288.46: If men achieve release by anointing mud and ash will they be relea sed?
288.47: Jackal, mouse and dear live in the forest and consume grass, leaves and water. Are they also ascetics?
288.48: From their birth to their death, frogs and fish stay in the river such as Ganga. Do they become Yogins?
288.49: Doves, l§ilaharas and Catakas do not drink water from the earth. Are they Vratins?
288.50: People are content with their routine work. But that does not help them to reach the goal. It is the knowledge of truth or reality that effects release.
288.51: O lord of birds, ignorant fools, fallen in the dark well of six darianas and bound by the noose of attachment, fail to realize the truth in the form of para-brahman.
288.52: Floating on the surface of the ocean in the form of Veda-sastra and caught by the waves of six nigrahas, the bad logicians suffer miserably.
288.53: A person well versed in the Vedas, Agamas and Puranas but ignorant of Reality is not distinct from a magician whose utterances resemble the caw'-caw sound of a crow.
288.54: Those who are worried about the sources and objects of knowledge take recourse to l§astras which they study day and night but they are miles away from the goal of Ultimate Truth.
288.55: Literary compositions arc decorated by the figures of speech, syntactical arrangement of words and by variety of meters. The fools who are worried cannot derive any solace from them.
288.56: A few proud people without traditional knowledge misinterpret the Vedas which they do not rightly understand.
288.57: They study the Vedas and discuss. But they do not realize the Ultimate Reality just as a spoon does not know the taste of food.
288.58: The head carries the flowers, the nose knows the scent. The people study the Vedas. But very few persons understand the same.
288.59: Not knowing the Reality of the self, a fool is infatuated by the sastras. When the goat stands in the shed, the shepherd seeks for it in the well in vain.
288.60: For the ignorant person the study of Sastras is useless as a mirror is useless for the blind. But for the wise the same works as the means of true knowledge.
288.61: Iastras are the source of knowledge which one desires to attain. But that is not an easy affair. One may not achieve knowledge even in one thousand divine years.
288.62: Having studied the Vedas and realized their essence the wise man should leave all the fastras just as one desiring corn leaves the husk.
288.63: Just as one satiated with nectar has no use of food, no one who is in search of Reality has anything to do*with the iastras.
288.64: One cannot obtain release by reading the Vedas or the astras. Release comes from experience, not otherwise, O son ofVinata.
288.65: The word of Guru alone can grant release. All knowledge is in vain. Among thousands of scriptures the word of Guru alone is vivifying.
288.66: The knowledge of the non-dual entity derived from the word of Guru can effect release. The practice of the ritual or the study of the crores of scriptures is quite in vain.
288.67: Some seek for the knowledge of non-dual brahman (i.e. brahman without Maya) and some for that of the Dual (brahman with Maya). But they do not realize reality devoid of dvaita and advaita.
288.68: Two words mine [mama) and not mine [na mama) signify bondage and release. By mine the person is bound and by not mine he is released.
288.69: So far as actions thrive, so far as desire subsists, so far as organs are active, there can be little talk of realizing the Self.
288.70: So far as one takes pride in body, so far as affection for worldly objects is there, so far there is persistence in efforts, so far as desire to do is there.
288.71: Penance, vow, pilgrimage, muttering of mantras sacrifice, worship, talk of the Vedas and Sastras are meaningful only when one knows Reality.
288.72: Therefore, by all efforts and in all conditions, focus your attention on atmariy O bird, if you desire release.
288.73: Tortured by the threefold suffering one should take shelter in the shade of the tree of moksa which has blossoms of dharma and knowledge and fruits of heaven and release.
288.74: Therefore, one should derive knowledge of Reality from one's preceptor. Thus one is easily released from the bondage of one's actions.
288.75: Now, hear, I shall tell you the last step by which one can attain the final goal.
288.76: When the hour of great departure arrives he should without fear cut off all attachments with the weapon of detachment.
288.77: The calm man should leave the house, start on pilgrimage and bathe in the holy waters. Then having prepared a seat as prescribed he should sit upon it with detachment.
288.78: With a pure mind he should meditate upon the pure, three-syllabled Om signifying brahman. Without forgett¬ ing the brahma-bija one should conquer the breath and control the mind.
288.79: He should control the organs from the objects of senses with intellect as his companion. The mind drawn away  by the actions should be possessed for the good by the intellect.
288.80: "I am brahman the supreme shelter. I am brahman the highest stage," having thus concluded he should concen¬ trate his personal self on the universal self.
288.81: Pronouncing Om the one-syllabled brahman and remembering me whosoever leaves his body obtains the highest state.
288.82: Where the hypocrites devoid of knowledge and self-control do not reach, the wise obtain that state.
288.83: The wise who are without ego and infatuation who have left attachment and vices, who contemplate on soul, whose desires have turned back, who are free from the effects of joy and sorrow, attain that imperishable state.
288.84: He obtains release who bathes in the holy tirtha of mind whose pond is knowledge, water is truth and wich is devoid of filth of attachment and envy.
288.85: Whosoever meditates on me with full devotion without attachment for any worldly object, who has imbibed complete awareness and whose mind is all pleasure.
288.86: With a desire to die whosoever leaves his house and stays in a holy place where he breathes his last, can obtain release.
288.87: Ayodhya, Mathura, Maya, Kaii, Kahci, Avantika Puri and Dvaravati—these seven places of pilgrimage can grant release.
288.88: Thus I have told you, O Garuda, about the ways of release. Preaching the same with knowledge and control, one may obtain release.
288.89: Those who have realized self can get release. Those who resort to the ritual can go to heaven. Those w'ho commit sins go to hell. Others rotate on the wheel of birth and death.
288.90: Thus, having received the answer of his queries from the mouth of the lord, Garuda was delighted and he bowed to the lord of the world.
288.91: "My doubts have been cleared, O lord, by your words"—so saying he took leave of Visnu and went to the hermitage of Kayapa.
288.92: One may assume body sooner or later after death. There is no inconsistency in this approach.
288.93: The Bhagavadgit& declares that after leaving the worne-out or diseased body the soul enters the new one immediately, as a man discarding worne-out clothes puts on new ones. But this is not true of each and every individual soul. Some souls wander in aerial bodies for indefinite time, some go to heaven, some to hell, staying in either place till their merits or sins are exhausted (kifie pur.ye martyaloikaTh vijanti). Some enter the womb very soon, to reap the fruits of their actions in human, animal or other form on the globe of this earth. «. '
288.94: Gania repeated what he had heard from the lord. Marica was also delighted on hearing the words of Lord Visnu.
288.95: O brahmanas, I have removed your doubts and told you the most wonderful Purana known as Garuda.
288.96: A man who hears the same or narrates the same is blessed with pleasure here as well as hereafter.
288.97: Whatsoever sorrows having been told about them who go to the city of Yama, whosoever hears about them gets release.
288.98: After hearing about the results of actions described here, men may become averse to pleasures. The account is, therefore, meaningful for the listener.
288.99: O ye that have controlled your organs, praise the lord from whom this voice has come out like a stream of nectar, by drinking (or hearing) even a drop or a handful of syllables of which a man may attain union with Paramatman.
288.100: The sages were fully satisfied having drunk the Vaisnavi nectar of words coming out of the mouth of Suta, replete with the essence of scriptures.
288.101: They praised the Suta who knew the essence of the iastras.
288.102: Thus having heard through the mouth of Suta the words of lord Vi§nu allaying the doubts of Garuda the sage Saunaka was fully satisfied.
288.103: The sages honoured Suta with liberal praise saying, *'0 Suta you deserve a very high praise." Then they bade him farewell, the sacrifice being over.
288.104: This holy Garuda Purana destroys sins committed by the listeners. This should be heard therefore.
288.105: Having heard the Purana, gifts of bed, etc., should be given in charity or else it would not be fruitful.
288.106: First of all, this Purana should be worshipped, 4hen the reciter with the fee in cash, clothes, ornaments and cows.
288.107: To obtain merit the reciter should be honoured devoutly with gifts of gold, corn, earth and other things.

289.1: The lord of Yadavas,* accompanied by his elder brother Balarama, looked splendid in the battle-field—the lord who was a thunderbolt to the enemy, the best and the noblest among men, cupid incarnate to the women, kith and kin of the cowherds, chastiser of the wicked kings, a loving child to his parents, Yama to the lord of Bhojas as ordained by fate, the transcendental soul for meditation on the part of Yogins.*
289.2: Salutation to lord Narayana, the source of the universe. After paying due homage to the lord, I shall narrate his story.
289.3: The great sages, aunaka and others preached spirituality and practised penance in the holy region of Naimisa.*
289.4: Vrfpfndm pati —lord of tUc descendents of Vrsni, an ancestor of lord Kr$na.
289.5: Lord >s called the greatest of Yogins (Yoglsvara).
289.6: They had conquered their senses, regulated their diet, were devoted to truth. They worshipped Vi?nu, the primeval preceptor of the universe with supreme devotion.

291.1: God Visnu had a desire to create beings worthy of creation, lo release beings worthy of release. Visnu ever cherishes such desires, though the expression of such desires is expressedly material.
291.2: Hari assumed a material form and swallowed dark¬ ness. That form of the lord they declare to be material. Those who do not know this enter the pitch dark region.
291.3: The incarnations of lord Visnu are perfect. Perfect is that supreme form. Perfection begets perfection.
291.4: Superiority and inferiority rest on personality, not on the facilities of Space and Time.
291.5: It has become a custom to say that he incarnates in the person ofKrsna for lightening the burden of the eardi. There can be no dissolution of the world without his wishes.
291.6: Too much effort should not be made for realizing Self. Too much effort made for self-realization occasions trouble. Too much eHbrt leads to certain disease, it is certain.
291.7: The teacher and the disciple should make common
291.8: O son of Vinata, those who think upon the lord as Supreme Reality are the teacher and the taught in the right sense of the word.
291.9: If the disciple cuts joke with the teacher out of ridicule or rage, if the teacher makes an ironical remark—the disciple and the teacher go to hell where they stay as long as the moon and the stars shine in the sky.
291.10: O Hari, please tell us about the nature of your energy and its constituents. Is that energy the very nature of yours or is it a separate entity? Tell me, O lord, as you know the truth.
291.11: O son of Vinata, the energy which lord Hari deposited in Maya is the very nature of the lord. The wise who know the truth have declared thus.
291.12: I'hey have also declared that the energy being material is a separate entity, like the lotus in the navel of Visnu. This fact is not detrimental to the concept of the lord being full of energy, as tlie lord is the very form of knowledge.
291.13: The people in general regard him as twofold: of the form of male and of the form of female. The two should not be considered to be separate entities, O lord of birds.
291.14: If the lord were separate from the female form, O lord of birds, how could the woman be his reflection.
291.15: Those seeking for release should know that Laksmi can never remain without Visnu in any space or time.
291.16: Lord Visnu deposits energy in her to further growth of creation. The asuras hold that energy is the magical power of the Lord. But they are fools who ignore reality and as a result enter the region of pitch darkness.
291.17: But if she be an empirical reality, how can she be eternal and if she be non-eternal, O lord of birds, how can she be the cause of creativity in her subtle form?
291.18: If she be the cause of creativity in the subtle form, who can be the cause of creativity in the gross form?
291.19: If you say: By the power of illusion, Visnu manifests himself in many forms. But when illusion disappears by knowledge, the universe (of various forms) is absorbed in Visnu. O lord of birds, hear, I shall produce an argument.
291.20: Hari, being omniscient, how can ignorance abide with him? As darkness cannot co-exist with the sun, there can be no ignorance co-existing with the lord.
291.21: How could the Vedas declare the identity of the two who are of contrary nature. Not circumscribed by space and time, the creator of the universe is omnipotent and is above all sorrows.
291.22: The devotees of Visnu and their followers are exempt from censure and reproach. He who bears malice to them cannot receive the pleasure of Visnu. Even in the state of release he cannot enjoy perfect bliss.
291.23: Those who perceive a difference between the Supreme and the subservient Self become subject to reproach and are overpowered by suffering and afflicted by affliction. They enter the region of pitch darkness whence there can be no return.
291.24: O lord of birds, the primordial nature (Prakrti) is subtle in form. It has the nature of eternal truth as are the infinitesimal particles of space, time, air and other elements.
291.25: O Krsna, O Madhava, O lord of Satvatas, you say that the ultimate particle of a substance is paramanu.
291.26: There are experts who can perceive the divisible particles of a substance but not the ultimate particle.
291.27: The sages declare the ultimate particle to be Viicsa. Following the view of ancient sages, the philosophers Kanada* and Gautama,® O lord of birds, have indorsed that the ultimate Visesa called Paramanu is indivisible.
291.28: The infinitesimal particles are divisible. Those who declare them indivisible are totally wrong in their view. Therefore, O son of Vinata,® the particles are divisible in many parts.
291.29: Kaudda or Katabhtd or Kaoabhakfa —the names of the founder of the Vaiie;ika system, which may be said to be a doctrine of atoms.
291.30: O lord of birds, the infinitesimal particles arc divisible in many parts. There are, in the same way, many forms of lord Hari. These forms are divisible while the lord himself is indivisible.
291.31: Therefore, O Garuda, know that he incarnates in particular forms. His all-pervasive form (which does not incarnate) they call Narayaia.
291.32: Thus, in all conditions and in all entirety, there is a fivefold classification of the different forms of the lord, viz., the eternal and non-eternal, the animate and inanimate and the lord circumscribed and not circumscribed by time, space and attributes. Lord Hari, the primeval Purua of mighty power, deposited energy in the primordial nature called Maya* and produced creation characterized by three gunas, viz.,sattva, rajas and tamas.

292.1: When the lord created the three gunas, their com¬ posite form being PrakrtP, there sprang up Laksmi in Iier threefold form, viz., Sri, Bhu and Durga.
292.2: O lord ot birds, one should not recognize any difference among Sri, Bhu, Durga—the three forms of Laksmi.
292.3: Those who recognize difference among the three, by virtue of three distinct gunas are thrown in the pitch dark regions.
292.4: Visnu pervaded the universe to sustain people with sattva guna. He inspired Brahma to create beings with rajas guna.
292.5: Brahma created the universe with rajas guna. Hence, Brahma is the first creator and not Visnu.
292.6: Brahma and Rudra are pervaded by Visnu. This very knowledge leads one to release. It is never otherwise.
292.7: They should recognize the respective functions of the three: Brahma, Visnu and Rudra. Those who do not recognize the same go to terrific hells whence there is no return.
292.8: The eternal lord Visnu pervaded the gunas, and activated them for the purpose of creation.
292.9: Equilibrium of the three guQai—Sattva, Rajas and Tamas—is called Praktti: sattva-rajas-tamasSth sflmyavasthi prakftil.
292.10: When the three gunas were activated there was evolved Mahat out of the constituents of the three gunas.
292.11: Out of Mahat were evolved Brahma and Vayu. They were born twins after the lapse of a year since Mahat came into being.
292.12: Mahat being activated by rajas, the creation was evolved out of the gunas in the state of imbalance.
292.13: O son of Devaki, you have explained to me the nature of creation evolved out of the gunas. I have gained by your grace the correct knowledge of the principle of Mahat in imbalance.
292.14: Thus I have explained to you, O lord of birds, the nature of the gunas, their number and the way how they function.
292.15: O son of Vinata, with the ten aggregated parts of tamas is mixed rajas in one tenth part.
292.16: Poison mixed with milk or sacrificial oblation is nothing but poison, the same is the position of gunas, O bird.
292.17: O lord of birds, when the gunas are mixed in equal proportion, the learned declare it to be the equilibrium of gunas.
292.18: Those who think otherwise, are placed in the pitch dark regions.
292.19: O lord, tell me, in brief, how the aggregated gunas stand in equilibrium, at the time of final dissolution {pralaya ).
292.20: The learned declare that the aggregated gunas stand in equilibrium, being mixed together.
292.21: Thus, the principle of mahat consists of four parts, being the form of Brahma himself which the learned declare to be due to the imbalance of gunas.
292.22: Thus, the three parts of rajas and one part of tamas constitute the body of Brahma due to the imbalance of gunas.
292.23: Mahat consists of four parts, of which the three arc rajas, one is tamas—this is what you have declared to me.
292.24: O lord, it appears from your statement that the body of Brahma is constituted of rajas.
292.25: In the threefold rajas of twelvefold agegafe, there exists sattva tenfold more in proportion to tamas.
292.26: In the threefold rajas of twelvefold aggregate there exists tamas elevenfold more in proportion to tamas.
292.27: Parts of rajas: One part of tamas, ten parts of rajas, one part of sattva—twelve parts in all.
292.28: Parts of tamas: One part of rajas, eleven parts of tamas.
292.29: Parts of sattva: Ten parts of sattva.

293.1: In the mahat principle, as described above, lord Visnu entered together with Laksnil and activated the same.
293.2: Characterized by the principle of ego, Sesa was evolv¬ ed at the beginning of creation. After the lapse of a thousand years, were born Siva and Garuda.
293.3: The eternal Visnu entered the ego. Lord Visnu and Lakml activated the ego.
293.4: I am threefold: of modified (i.e. secondary) form, born of tamas and of tejas. Lord Rudra is the controller of the three.
293.5: O lord of birds, from the mahat were evolved the presiding deities of eleven organs of sense.®
293.6: These were evolved from Sesa one after the other, within ten years serially.
293.7: Then were evolved Indra and Kama—the presiding deities of the mind. O Tarksya, bondage and release came afterwards.
293.8: EUi'ctt organs of sense —five organs of intellect and five organs of action and one mind.
293.9: Thereafter, the organ of perception came into being.
293.10: Iatarupa, wife of Svayambhuva Manu, Yama, Moon and Sun—the four presiding deities of their respective organs came into being.
293.11: Visvamitra, Vasistha, Atri, Marici, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Angiras and Vaivasvata Manu. Manu and others of endless number are the presiding deities of the generating organ.
293.12: O lord of birds, thereafter were born the presiding deities of anus. They arc:
293.13: Sviyamhhuoa Manu.: Bom of Brahmi and Satarupa he is known as the author of the Manusmrti.
293.14: Now, I shall tell you the names of seven Vasus: Drona, Prana, Dhruva, Arka, Dosa, Vasu, Vibhavasu being the seventh.
293.15: Rudras are ten in number. The primary Rudra is called Bhava. O best of birds, now I shall tell you the ten names of Rudra.®
293.16: Raivanteya, Bhlrna, Vamadeva, Vrsakapi, Ahirbu- dhnya, Bahurupa, Mahan.
293.17: The rest of the Puraias mention eleven Rudras. The present Puraqa mentions ten but gives only seven names.
293.18: An obvious departure from ancient tradition which mentions twelve Adityas. A number of names in these lists do not corresnd with the names of this hst.
293.19: Excluding Visvaksena, Jaya and the rest are the councillors. In their mutual relationship some are equal and some unequal.
293.20: These arc the secondary controllers of the organs of sense. Hence, they are inferior to the presiding deities of the tattvas.
293.21: O lord of birds, I shall now tell you about Jaya etc., who came after Visvaksena. In the materialistic creation Agni stands first. Cyavana son of sage Bhrgu and Utathya son of Brhaspati come after agni.
293.22: Seven groups of manes were created thereafter, O lord of birds.
293.23: Rbhus are a group of divine beings who attained divinity by performing tapas. RV. 1.111 mentions one Angiras, the son of BrahmS who had a son named Sudhanva. Sudhanva had three children: Rbhusan, Vibhvas and Vaja. The three were names of Rbhus.
293.24: The three groups of Pitfs include Agnisvattas, Barhisadas and Somapas.
293.25: Manus are fourteen in number. They are Svayambhuva (2) Sva- rocia, (3) Uttama, (4) Tamasa, (5) Raivata, (6) Gaksu$a, (7) Vaivasvata, (8) S&varni, (9) Dharma, (10) Sivariika (II) Pisahga, (12) Apisahgabha, (13) 8abala, (14) Varaka. But the present Pur&ra mentions only eleven. The Pur&Qas differ in the number and nomenclature of Manus.

294.1: O lord, I bow to your lotus-feet. I have no resort except the shelter of your feet. Your lordship possesses Virtue, Some 1 have known, some I have not.
294.2: Please give me shelter. Protect me from dangers. There is none more delightful, none more endearing than your lordship.
294.3: "O lord of Laksmi, an abode of living beings, you are the ocean of knowledge and omniformed. Where am I with my limited knowledge and full of ignorance and where your lord- ship all-powerful and omniscient. I am ignorant with my circumscribed knowledge. So is Her Ladyship Laksmi.
294.4: I have very little knowledge, very little devotion and very little detachment. And whatever little I possess is also due to your favour. There too, O Visnu, who are an abode of the universe, I have no ownership.
294.5: O lord, eschew my ego and attachment to worldly affairs. I desire nothing more. I deserve the attainment of right knowledge. I am not a negligent or an imprudent pupil.
294.6: Let my organs of senses that are inclined to move in wrong channels fall at your lotus-feet. I am inferior to Laksmi by millions of virtues, I have no capacity to sufficiently praise your merits. Be pleased, O lord.'*
294.7: Thus with palms joined in reverence Brahma praised the lord in the presence of Garuda. Then, the god of gods, the noble Vayu was visibly moved to love and devotion at the sight of the lord.
294.8: With eyes overflowing with tears and speech characterized in faltering accents he began to praise the lord.
294.9: O lord of Laksmi, I beg the favour of yours granting me the four objects of human life, O lord.
294.10: "O lord, you incarnate for rendering favour to the people who are averse to devotion, who are given to sinful acts and who are terribly suffering from (threefold) affliction. O lord, you have no other object of life.
294.11: O Vasudeva, out of mere sport, you incarnate in human form. You render welfare to the cows, brahmins, gods and the world of vegetation, tliat being the sole purpose of your incarnation on this earth.
294.12: O lord, you are the foremost of pious activators. O lord of the mind-born god, the consort of Rati®, our mind, engaged in praise of your merit, finds no satiation whatsoever.
294.13: O Mukunda, I am your steadfast devotee. Pray create devotion in me for your lotus-feet. This and nothing else do I crave of you.
294.14: O god of gods, in whatever station you are present, let me also be there by your favour. Conversely, in whatever station I am present, let your presence be also there, O lord. This is my utmost desire. The four-faced Brahma alone is aware of it.
294.15: O lord, let my subconscious mind be also at your worship; let my activities be your circumambulation, let my behavioral conduct also be your praise. O lord, I offer all these to you with my conscious mind.
294.17: The material substances intended for my use are nothing but different forms of Hari. O God of gods, I always regard these to be such» and worship the same with proper devotion.
294.18: The Sandal paste, fragrant flowers, the incense, the clothes, the eatable food-stuff—all these are for the pleasure of Visnu. I undertake this vow for the gratification of Visnu.
294.19: I abhor the non Vaisnava people and love the Vaisnava ones. I cut off the tongue of the people who reproach lord Visnu. With the heated liquefied tin I fill the ears of those who hear his reproaches.
294.20: O God, by your favour I possess sufficient strength for the purpose. Still I lack in strength to offer sufficient prayers. I am inferior to Laksmi by millions of virtues.
294.21: I crave for eternal pleasure accruing from the company of the person who sings praises of Hari. Those who unitiate others to the same are Vaisnavas attached to Visnu.
294.22: Thus, the noble Baladeva eulogized lord Hari and stood in front of him with palms joined in reverence.
294.23: O god of gods, you are praised by Brahma and other gods. Your merits entering the ear-hole of a person destroy our attachment for the body that is the cause of our rebirth.
294.24: Your praise, O lord, destroys our attachment not only for the body but also for our home, wife, sons, etc., and for fields, animals, gems or other precious articles.
294.25: Though the Vedas have tried to explain your identity (they have not done it fully). Laki too has failed to
294.26: I cannot sufficiently praise you, O lord. I am inferior to Brahma and Vayu. Hence, be merciful and protect me, O lord."
294.27: O lord of birds, thus Sarasvat! praised Hari and became silent. Thereafter, Bharat! began to praise lord Hari.
294.28: I have, therefore, strong desire to praise your virtues, O lord.
294.29: When sorrows are removed, the deserving devotee enjoys fruits of pleasure. The absence of devotion, on the contrary, invites sin and destroys virtue.

300.10: Still Laksmi does not know your traits in entirety. Nothing remains which the Vedas have not covered up. There are yet some distinct traits which are not expressed by the Vedas.

303.1: Lord Hari, the primeval being, thought of incarnat¬ ing himself. He appeared as Visnu, the repository of all virtuous deeds.
303.2: Lord Visnu, the germ of all creation, incarnated as Vasudeva. He entered the womb of Maya and created Vayu.
303.3: He created Mahat (in subtle form) with sixteen digits accompanied by ego. I shall now tell you the sixteen digits.
303.4: The lord then became Sanandana and in that form he practised celibacy and subdued the ten organs of senses, a
303.5: Five gross elements: earth, water, fire, wind and ether.

303.10: Lord Visnu became a hog' and took the earth out of waters. He slew Hiranyaksa, protected the pious and established rule of law over the earth.
303.11: The lord incarnated himself as Mahidasa from his mother Yamini and father who was not a sage. In his incar¬ nation as Mahidasa he preached philosophy of Paficaratra.
303.12: The lord became Kapila,* explained tattvas, removed doubts and instructed Asuri.®

304.1: O lord of birds, now, listen to the nature of Maha- laksmi, her incarnations and the extent of knowledge peculiar to her.
304.2: Brahma and Vayu are inferior to Visnu by millions of qualities. Now, I shall tell you about the nature of Brahman, O lord of birds.
304.3: Bom of Lord Vi§riu and his consort Maya, Brahma is called Viriflca.
304.4: Bom of Aniruddha and his consort iSanta, and constituted of intellect ( Mahat ), he obtained the appellation— Mahaviriflca.
304.5: Born ofVasudeva from Maya by rajas, he (Viriflci) is called Vidhi.
304.6: Bom of Universal egg from the navel lotus of Visnu and seated in the lotus itself, he is called Caturmukha—the four¬ faced god, O best of birds.
304.7: Thus they declare the four names of Brahma. I shall now tell you the names of Vayu, O lord of birds.
304.8: Vayu abides in the hearts of all people—this is what Lord Vinu has declared Hence, he is called Mukti.
304.9: With my consent, he confers liberation to his devotees by imparting knowledge to them. V4yu is called mukti.
304.10: Abiding in the hearts of his devotees he multiplies their devotion for Visnu. Therefore, he is called the devotee of Visnu.
304.11: He constitutes the consciousness of living beings. He is called consciousness.
304.12: Staying in the heart of the people, O lord, he observes their strength. O lord of Vinata, he is, therefore, called Bala.
304.13: Abiding in the hearts of people he conducts sacrifices through their sons and grandsons. He is, therefore, called a sacrificer.
304.14: Among the sages too, those who worship Hari for attaining the object of their desire are called anrjus. The same practice is current among the people.
304.15: [He cannot obtain release] until he gives up Hari's worship with an object in view, for desire is an obstacle in the path of realization, even for the sages.
304.16: Impressions of countless activities performed in previous ages are obstacles to the person seeking for liberation. He should, therefore, give up worship which aims at the fulfil¬ ment of desire.
304.17: By enlightenment received from Guru's instructions all activities practically cease to be. Being initiated in Yoga and practising the same, the aspirant achieves liberation after all.
304.18: The worship of the lord with an object in view imparts riches which controvert knowledge and lead to darkness.
304.19: Stationed in the heart of devotees and showing them what is wholesome and what is not, he is called Guru.
304.20: Stationed in the heart of Yogins and meditating on the lord as a distinct entity he is called a meditator.
304.21: As he comprehends the lord according to his ability and as he knows the qualities abiding in Rudra and other gods he is called Vijfla, O best of birds.
304.22: When the results of virtue and sin are exhausted, the gods, as far as Vayu, deserve perfect bliss.
304.23: As Vayu creates objects of enjoyment for the pleasure of gods, sages and nobles, he is called joyful.
304.24: Human soul suffers from affliction caused by the Daityas. People suffer often and anon specially in the Kali age.
304.25: Vayu consumes all sorrows accruing both from virtue and vice in the Kali age. Hence, Vayu is called Kali.
304.26: O lord, whatever joys or pleasures accrue to the people are due to divine influences. There is not in the least any doubt in this.
304.27: O son of Vinata, Devas do not go to hell, and Daityas do not seek pleasure from the objects of pleasihre.
304.28: Vayu enjoys the fruits of his virtuous deeds. He suffers from his sinful actions. It is hard to escape the results of good or bad activities.
304.29: Partial incarnations of Lord Vayu from Prana to Sukha arc nineteen in number. O lord of birds, the lord has descended on earth several times, each time with a separate identity.
304.30: When lord Rama incarnated on earth, Vayu was born as Hanuman for rendering assistance to Rama.
304.31: Then he will be born as the son of Vasudeva. There will be none equal to him in the fourteen worlds.* He will be fully equipped with wisdom.
304.32: The fourteen worlds are divided into two groups: seven higher and seven lower regions. Bhu, Bhuvah, Svah, Mahah, Janah, Tapas, Satya, or Brahma are the upper regions rising from the earth, one above the other; while Atala, Vitala, Satala, Ras§tala, Talitala, Mahatala and PatSla are the lower regions descending from the earth, one below the other.
304.33: The full incarnations of Vayu are three. Their creed is one and the same which is propounded in the Bhagavata.
304.34: In the four incarnations, at the hour of birth, the lord, at first, dries up the embryo before he is born out of the womb.
304.35: In the Kfta age, there were born from Pradyumna twins Savitri and Sarasvati.
304.36: These are the three forms of Vani. I shall now tell you about the incarnations of Bhdrati. Please hear attentively.
304.37: Being the presiding deity of the Vedas she is the Veda itself. She is the mistress of Vayu, the great meditator.
304.38: She presents all objects of senses to lord Visnu for propitiating him or for his enjoyment. Hence, she is called Bhuji.
304.39: She became the mistress of Citra. In the name of Sraddha she became the mistress of lord Rocana.
304.40: O lord of birds, Hanuman, the son of Vayu, lived in the Treta age. Then, Bharati was born as the daughter of a Brahmin,!iva by name.
304.41: Not only Bharati and her companions such as Saci, etc., but also all the rest who were born of him were married to their partners.
304.42: Bharati, the daughter of Kasiraja known by her popular name Kali became the mistress of Bhimasena.
304.43: Draupadi, the daughter of Drupada, gave up her body together with her maidens. O lord of birds, she will be born in the Kali age in the house of l§ankara in the village of Karati.
304.44: She died as a maiden to become the mistress of Vayu in her third birth.
304.45: O good one, such are the mistresses of Vyu and Brahma. O lord of birds, they are inferior to their husbands in hundreds of merits.

305.1: O lord of birds, O noble one, I shall tell you the reason thereof. Please listen.
305.2: In the presence of Brahma, they displayed their amorous feelings. O best of birds, on seeing that they were excited by love, Brahma cursed all the four.
305.3: "Since you are excited by love, you will be born as mortals and will marry the mortals."
305.4: In the second birth, you will be born as human beings but turn unchaste. In the third birth you will be born as human beings and married to men with whom you will remain for life.
305.5: In the fourth birth, as in the first, you will not turn unchaste and you will not be separated from your husbands.
305.6: Thus cursed by Brahma, the four ladies discussed the matter among themselves on the peak of Meru. They said:
305.7: "The curse of Brahma cannot be nullified, though we make hundreds of attempts. Association of the divine with the human is not commendable. It brings misfortune.
305.8: "O ladies of good vow, wherefore do you worship me?" Being devoted to her, they expressed their woes thus.
305.9: Now, that we shall be united with human beings we shall not incur the sin of unchastity if we unite ourselves with Vayu. O Bharat!, we desire to be identical with you in these births.
305.10: Thus urged by the ladies, O best of birds, Bharat! agreed to their request and descended to the earth together with those ladies.
305.11: Since urged by Parvat! you have displayed amours to lord Brahma, Parvat! will be considered to be the best amongst you all.
305.12: Even though she remains in the company of lord Kfsna, she will not be sexually united with him.
305.13: Thus, lord Hari, stationed in the heart of Rudra, conferred boon to the ladies and disappeared.
305.14: When the lord had left for his celestial abode, the ladies gave up their physical bodies and were born as daughters to king Nala and were named Indrasena and others.
305.15: They went to forest (for living an ascetic's life) but fell in love with Sage Mudgala at first sight.
305.16: At the same time, Vayu intervened and overpowered Mudgala. Vayu copulated with Bharati and her companions.
305.17: While she lived as Kr?na she had the recollection that she was in fact Bharati. Saci and others too recollected their original Self but only sometimes.
305.18: When Parvati indulged in intercourse with her husband she had no such idea. She thought she was indulging in love-sport in a dream.
305.19: Similarly, Bharati had no intercourse with Yudhi¬ sthira, Arjuna and others, since they could not copulate with a mortal.
305.20: The gods know some peculiar ways of copulation, of which the mortals are quite ignorant.
305.21: When Bharati, etc. in the form of DraupadI are copulating, their male partners are divine beings, not human ones. Hence, their copulation with human beings such as Arjuna is not untenable.

306.1: I shall now tell you about the subsidiary creation for your knowledge. Please, hear attentively and retain the same in your memory, O lord of birds.
306.2: Sea served as a couch, though lord Hari did not need it.
306.3: I am always your devotee. I shall remain so in each and every birth of mine*".
306.4: Thus, Garuda served as the Vehicle of lord Hari. Garuda was the son of Vayu called Sfitra. Bom of Vinata he was popularly known as Vainateya.
306.5: O lord of birds, identical with ego, you were born of Virifica identical with intellect. The propitiation of Hari has been the mission of your life.
306.6: O lord, the three are at par with one another but are superior to Gayatri and Bharati in respect of virtues.
306.7: O lord, born of Sumitra and Dasaratha, Laksmana was the incarnation of Sesa having certain ariisas of Vayu and Ananta.
306.8: I shall now tell you the incarnations of Rudra. Hear attentively, O lord of birds.
306.9: Rudra identical with ego obtained the title 'ever- inauspicious' and was assigned the task of destruction.
306.10: As he ever wore the inauspicious garland of skulls, he was called ever-inauspicious. He should be ever distinguished from Siva, the devotee of Visnu.
306.11: Sometimes, influenced by the Asuras, he acted con¬ trary to the wishes of the lord, he was called ever-inauspicious. As such, he should be distinguished from Siva, the devotee of lord Visnn.
306.12: To practise penance, he remained in the salt-ocean for ten divine years. Hence, he obtained the title tapasj O lord of birds.
306.13: Suka, the son of Vyasa, who had been influenced by Vayu was the incarnation of Rudra. He was born for the spread of knowledge in the world.
306.14: Stationed in the north-eastern direction, Rudra obtained the title of Vamadeva. Stationed to the left of Vayu, he is propitiated by him, his worthy disciple.
306.15: Hence, Rudra got the title of Vamadeva. Further, on the strength of his lordship and nobility he obtained the titles of Kala and Bala and not by the virtue of his hand¬ some features.
306.16: To slay the Asuras of Tripura who were inimical to Visnu, Rudra assumed the form of Aghora. Hence, he is called Aghora.
306.17: To confer boon to the daityas who had followed the path of service and practised penance, Rudra was born in a trice and was called Sadyojata.
306.18: O lord, please tell me why Sage Oru wept in devotion and why his son Aurva tried to revive the cult of weeping.
306.19: O lord of good vow, I, your grandson, desire to hear all this in detail. Being addressed by Garuda, the compas¬ sionate lord spK)ke in reply.
306.20: Rudra saw his own self reflected in Sahkarsana who was possessed of good qualities, whose lotus-feet were bowed to by Brahma, Sesa and others desirous of gaining victory (over the senses), as well as by Bharati and Svastipas.
306.21: With his body shivering with fear Rudra wept and spoke to the lord again.
306.22: My very sight b productive of sin. My very speech b attended by sin. My very eyes are set on women, instead of being set on you.
306.23: I have been attached to my children, wife and other
306.24: O lord of many ears, I did not hear your narrative with attention. Conversely, I have been indulging in gossip with the lay people. By what merit have I seen you, O lord?
306.25: Seeing the footstool whereon the lord had put his feet, Rudra had his throat choked with emotion. He wept while his body shivered with fear, thinking how could he hear the narrative of the lord.
306.26: O lord! how could I touch your body. O man-lion stationed at the tip of nose, O lord of nose, 1 have not smelt the fragrance of fresh lotuses. If I have smelt, I have not offered the same to you.
306.27: By what merits, O lord, have I seen your face with lovely nose and shining teeth.
306.28: With his body shivering with fear, Rudra wept and said: O lord, how do I breathe out the smell of flowers that hud been left after they were offered to you?
306.29: O lord Jihva, as you always sit on the tongue (of the faithful), if a person in the presence of your image takes bath every day in the water containing the remains of the eatables that had been mixed with Tulasi leaf offered to you, that has been sprinkled over with the water wherewith your feet have been washed, though the offering of the eatable has been made just by word of mouth, obtains the merit of performing ten thousand crores of sacrifices.
306.30: Such remains of eatables, as luminous as the Sun, I have neither eaten nor offered to you. I have taken meals but not offered the same to you.
306.31: I have not offered any eatable at your lotus-feet. By what merit have I seen you, O lord?
306.32: I saw your head adorned with diadem and curly hair being the support of heaven and earth. I have seen your face by the aggregate of merit accumulated in my several previous births, in the company of noble people.
306.33: Alas! O lord, it will disappear again by the aggre¬ gate of sins accumulated in my several previous births.
306.34: O omniformed lord, your lotus-feet kept in the heart by the great Yogins, have been seen by me out of com¬ passion. O Vasudeva, how shall I see them again. Thus Rudra wept again.
306.35: I saw your belly in the field of battle containing three worlds. I saw your body adorned with discus, conch, etc., which could stop the recurrence of birth. O lord of Laksmi, how could I see it over and over again.
306.36: How shall I see you again and again? Thus, out of devotion, Rudra wept and wept again. Thus Rudra obtained the title Oru and his son obtained the title Aurva.
306.37: Since he made Rudra fertile, the son of Rudra was named Aurva. Aurva saw people worthy of liberation as well as engrossed in the objects of senses.
306.38: Aurva praised the lotus-feet of Vi$nu, remembered them again and again and felt choked in the throat. These sinners employ their senses to evil objects every day.
306.39: Aurva, with his body shivering with fear remembered Maya of the lord and wept.
306.40: These men of wicked nature accumulate wealth with great effort. These animals (in the garb of human beings) earn with great toil without any return.
306.41: Deluded by the Mayaof Visnu, these wealthy people do not part with their wealth in favour of a worthy person who can be equated with the lord. The noble have declared their life to be a wastage. Thus sorrowful at their loss Rudra cried aloud.
306.42: Let my family live for hundred years. Let my sons live for hundred years. Let me also live in comfort for hundred years. Let my auspicious wife too live for hundred years.
306.43: Let my cows always yield milk. Let me give my son to my daughter-in-law and my daughter to my son-in-law.
306.44: I shall marry my daughter in a noble and rich family. 1 shall give wealth to them on their marriage. Taking note of these people who are devoid of discernment, lord Vamadcva laughs at their folly.
306.46: Lord Vasudeva, designated as fortune confers fruits of acts to all and sundry, at the opportune time. Solely devoted to Vasudeva, Aurva saw these stupid people and wept.
306.47: But when Rudra married the daughter of Himadri he became attached to her. Hence, he got the designation Para.
306.48: Rudra had ten brothers. Among these, the three, viz. SadaSiva Saumitreya and Rauhineya—were inferior to Rudra and his consort by one himdred merits.
306.49: O compassionate lord, please tell me about the Eternal Bliss {dnanda)y explaining its nature to satisfy my curiosity and for enlightening the seekers after truth.
306.50: O lord, please tell me, since I am your disciple, just for lifting me up, and out of compassion for me. Since you are fully satiated, you have no desire to be fulfilled.

307.1: Goddess Laksmi too knows me in all my incarnations.
307.2: She knows my indivisible subtle qualities endowed with many specialities, through Brahma or by my grace.
307.3: Goddess Laksmi knows her own subtle form endowed by special traits.
307.4: Brahma too perceives the all-pervading Vasudeva endowed with noble qualities proportionately larger than those of Vayu. Ears do not know the qualities of the lord which are subtle and special.
307.5: Except lord Brahma even the gods, until and unless they are released, are ignorant. Brahma and Vayu know their Self and the Supreme Self endowed with special traits.
307.6: Sarasvati perceives my special qualities who am a seh born lord but not beyond my form as Kf na constituted of three gui!tas.
307.7: O lord of birds, 8esa and Rudra perceive me stationed in the tamoguna. But they do not know my other guas and their special traits. O dear, I have told you the truth.
307.8: Uma, Suparna and Varuni—the three know me very well as I am stationed (in their heart). But, O lord of birds, my special traits perceived by Rudra are not known to them at any place or time.
307.9: O lord of birds, Indra and other gods know me as peivading the Ego; Dak and other Prajapatis as pervading the intellect. So also Soma and Surya.
307.10: RukminT, etc. are my six principal queens. O lord of birds, amongst them Nila was the daughter of Agni in the pre¬ vious creation. I make no distinction in sexual enjoyment with them.
307.11: As a maiden she cherished to wed Krsna (my form), She relished what she conceived in mind. O lord of birds, Agni tried his best to marry her with one of the pitfs.
307.12: But the maiden did not agree to any proposal, her mind being extremely set on Krsna.
307.13: Then, the fire-god spoke to his daughter. O silly one, why don't you marry? Thereupon, the maiden spoke to her father thus.
307.14: The celestial women abandon their husbands and enjoy intercourse with the lord who stays with them (in heaven). As these women find their husbands in the lord, they are honoured by the people. There can be no second thinking in this respect.
307.15: If they get husbands devoted to Visnu, their life becomes fruitful. They can get husbar.ds devoted to Vinu by the aggregate of merits accumulated in several births.
307.16: If they have stored merit accruing from their pious acts performed In previous lives, their husbands can be devoted to Visnu.
307.17: Rare are the devotees of Vi$nu in Kali age. Rare is a devotion for the lord. Rare is the narrative of the lord to be heard in the mortal world. Initiation in the cult of Vi§nu is rare, very rare. Rare is the company of the devotees of Hari.
307.18: Rare are the people with faithful wives and worthy sons. Rare is the sight of the lord on the mountain Sesa. Rare is the sight of Rahganatha on the Kaveri.* Rare is the sight of the Ganges.®
307.19: Hence, I do not desire a husband other than lord Krsna. Having uttered such words to her father she went to the mountain Sesa.
307.20: To the north of it, at the distance of two Krosas at Mahatala, she commenced a great penance in a solitary pit.
307.21: She meditated upon Narayana for one thousand divine years. At the end of this period, she began to praise the lord.
307.23: O lord, ward off from my sight the people who have offended you, who have tried to frustrate my desire to become your devotee, who bear malice to their preceptors and your worshippers.
307.24: O lord, you ward off my talk with those who hate you. You establish my contact with your lotus feet. Homage to you, O lord who inhabit Sri Saila and who are the abode of Laksmi, your loving consort.
307.25: O lord of Laksmi, the superior and inferior, the pri¬ mary cause of creation, I have not seen you since long. Of you, the four-armed god, the vision is possible only by the aggre¬ gate of merits accumulated in several previous lives.
307.26: Polluted by all sorts of sins, O lord, how can I have your vision. O lord of birds, I am your devotee, the devotee of your devotees. O abode of the universe, be pleased with me.
307.27: Thus praised, the compassionate lord Varadaraja was pleased by her devotion. He appeared before her and said:
307.28: O good lady, express your desire. I have come to you to fulfil the same.
307.29: She spoke to Han, the abode of Laksmi and the lord of the universe with great devotion. O lord with a lovely face, may I become your wife.
307.30: On hearing her words, the lord spoke to her iji gentle words.

308.1: O lord of birds, Bhadra, the daughter of Nala, desired lord Visnu to be her husband. As she, who was auspicious by merit, worshipped and circumambulated the lord she was called Bhadra.
308.2: To Bhadra the maiden, the father Nala spoke thus. O Bhadra, why do you trouble your body (by worshipping the lord). What is the fruit of this suffering, tell me, O daughter.
308.3: Dear father, now hear. None can declare the gain derivable from paying homage to lord Visnu.
308.4: Even then, I shall tell you something, as far as I can, just for the welfare of the world. The compassionate lord Visnu is alone my guide. I am a slave of his slaves. May he protect me. I bow to his feet. Saying so, she prostrated at the feet of the lord.
308.5: The wise declare that homage to Hari, if it is not accompanied by the prescribed worship, is fruitless. O father, now, hear details. "One should bow to lord Visnu by reciting the formula: O lord of Rama, O lord of Madhu, O lord of Sarasvati, homage to thee."
308.6: (O father) the lord of lords is pleased not so much by worship as by offering homage to him or by reciting his name.
308.7: O father, people attain health and prosperity by offering homage to him. But such prosperity and good health are valueless. They occasion suffering in hell.
308.8: Offering homage to the lord and uttering his name are superior to the worship rendered unto him. Hence, one should pay homage to Visnu as well as utter his name, O father.
308.9: So far you have not rendered homage to the lord, not uttered his name. The hour of death is quite uncertain. Do not trust your body, O lord.
308.10: O lord of lords, Nala heard her speech simple and straightforward. He paid homage and at his best circumambu¬ lated the lord. She too did likewise.
308.11: Her five brothers Kaikeyas gave her to me in marriage, O best of birds.
308.12: I am going to tell you about the circumstances how Mitravinda was married. O noble lord of birds, now hear attentively.
308.13: In the previous creation Mitravinda performed at will several sacrifices, Agnisoma and others for attaining Hari as friend.
308.14: There being many ways to attain her purpose, Matravinda thought of a sure one. She found that the hearing of the SdUvika Puranas was the best way.
308.15: If they hear a Purana which contains no reference to Visnu, their life becomes miserable. Their baths of purification, their repetition of lord's name, their five great sacrifices, their observance of vows, their performance of Istapurta and Krcchra Gandrayana are rendered useless. All such perfor¬ mances are fruitless including the ceremony of initiation in the Vaisnava cult, though it may have been properly performed, if it is devoid of Hari's narrative.
308.16: The wise declare that the life of such people is render¬ ed fruitless as have not heard the Bhagavata or the Brahma- kanda of the present Purana, in the company of their preceptor or the 'followers' of the Bhagavata sect.
308.17: One should not linger even for a moment where there is no stream in the form of lord's narrative, no resort at the feet of Narayana, and no talk about the lord.
308.18: The ear adorned with the divine flowers looks not so beautiful as the one adorned by the ornaments in the form of Visnu's tale.
308.19: Those who clad in head dress and bodice hear or recite the narrative of the lord are alone worthy of respect in the world, not those who are addicted to vicious objects of senses.
308.20: Those who recite the Bhagavata Purana out of greed for riches or those who know but do not reveal the secret of the Bhagavata go to Yama's abode.
308.21: Those who are extremely greedy of wealth have no right to recite this Purana.
308.22: For the well-being of the people who regard lord Visnu and none else to be all-pervading, lord alone undertakes the charge.
308.23: The lord bestows the fruits of auspicious and inauspi¬ cious Karmans. One should never endeavour for the accumu¬ lation of wealth, rather one should fix one's mind in devotion for Visnu.
308.24: One should take bath for purification, recite sacred mantra, dispose articles of worship. Being purified thus, he who is well versed in the Puranas should recite regularly the Bhagavata Purana every day.
308.25: Acquisition of wealth, knowledge of the Vedas and astras and the narrative of Visnu come as a result of previous auspicious activities. Of these listening to Hari is very rare.
308.26: One should enjoy the essence of the Bhagavata Purana—a rare thing in this mortal world. One should enjoy the essence so that tears of joy may trickle down the eye—a phenomenon very rare to Occur.'
308.27: Since she obtained Hari as Mitra (as friend) I was named Mitravinda.
308.28: In the Svayamvara, Mitravinda discarded all candi¬ dates who had come to woo her and put garland around my neck as a token of acceptance. I then conquered all the kings and reached home with her. O lord of birds.

309.1: This penance has its root in remorse. O lord of birds, you may hear in detail.
309.2: I have not remembered the ambrosial name of Hari. Rather, I have remembered his faults. I have not thought upon the ambrosial essence of Hari's teachings. Rather, I have indulg¬ ed in gossips with the common people.
309.3: I have not worshipped the lotus-feet of Hari. On the other hand, I worshipped my sons and friends. I did not bow at the lotus feet of Hari. On the other hand, I worshipped the feet of my friends.
309.4: I have not seen the face of Hari covered with tresses grey as the incense smoke. I have fondled with my sons with affection and not caressed your loving face.
309.5: I have adorned my sons and friends with ornaments but not the face of my lord who can eschew the effects of my sins which I committed in my previous life.
309.6: I did not partake of the remanent of food offered to you but I partook of six varieties of food at the house of my friends. I did not offer you flowers and fragrances but did the same to my sons and friends. I am now tired of my sons and friends. When shall I sec your face, O lord?
309.7: I have polluted my tongue by consuming the prohibited vegetables not sanctified by mantras, a part of which has not been offered to you, which are not permitted in the coteries of your devotees and which are forbidden in the codes that prescribe rules of conduct. When shall I sec your face, O lord?
309.8: I have not purified my body by worshipping you with the eight-syllabled mantra or by visiting holy places or by blowing conches in front of your idol. When shall I see your face, O lord?
309.9: I have incurred sin by not offering perfumes and flowers, ornaments or clothes. My body is polluted by anoin¬ ting it with the perfumes prepared by those who are not the devotees of Visnu. When shall I sec your face, O lord?
309.10: O Vasudeva, my feet are burnt since they have not
309.11: My hands are burnt since they did not perlbrm your worship. I have incurred sin by indulging in sinful activities. When shall I see your face, O lord?
309.12: I have not attained even the slightest pleasure since I gave up your worship, in spite of the fact that I have my hus¬ band, sons, friends, servants, buildings, cattle and wealth. Hence¬ forth, I shall not visit my kins and friends. I shall ever remain your devotee, nay a slave.
309.13: Those who regard their kins and friends as the sources of joy have their faces filled with urine and faeces. This is what I know.
309.14: Whatever has passed so far, I have suffered utterly thereby. Please, favour me with the company of the noble by your grace and not with the company of the wicked by your indifference.
309.15: At that time, I had gone ahunting on the bank of Yamuna. I saw her there practicing penance. I spoke to my friend Arjuna.
309.16: O friend, approach the maiden immediately and ask her about (he purpose of her penance.
309.17: Thus asked, Arjuna approached her and asked her the purpose of her penance. After knowing her purpose, he returned and told me all that he had learnt of her. Then, at the auspicious hour, I married her.
309.18: I married just to favour her, but not for my pleasure, I shall now tell you the story of Laksmana and the reason why I married her.

310.1: O lord of birds, in her previous birth Laksmana was the daughter of a learned Brahmana Vahnideva. Since she possessed auspicious marks, she was called Sulakmana.
310.2: Brahma too has thirtytwo marks. So has Bharati. The same number of marks characterize Visnu. 1 shall tell you my decisive thought on this point.
310.3: O lord of birds, Laksmi knows the additional marks as compared with her own in the Vayu form of Vi?nu. Bharati has one hundred additional marks in comparison with her own.
310.4: In the absence of marks of eyes and brows, lord Hari contains anger; his penis and belly are somewhat larger in proportion.
310.5: A slight arrangement of the belly, small feet, short ears, long tufts, except in a Brahmana lady and in the consort of Siva, are regarded as great defects.
310.6: Thirtytwo marks of Visnu, Brahma has already explained with reference to himself.
310.7: Those stated by me or by Brahma are not contra¬ dictory to each other. Whatever I had stated I repeat succinctly.
310.8: I have stated these by collecting the scattered material together. As it is evident, there is no contradiction in what I have stated at other places in the text.
310.9: Lady Laksmana and others possess twenty-seven marks. In comparison to Bharati she is short of five marks in pudendum, ears, hands, breast and belly.
310.10: O lord of birds, she has neither the additional marks of gods, nor the additional marks of Rudra. She is possessed of twenty six marks minus six marks of Varuna, plus additional marks in ears, belly, nose, hair, ankle and pudendum.
310.11: Hari eats and drinks in the company of his friends. Therefore, a householder should gift sumptuous food and tasteful drink in favour of the lord and receive his blessing. Otherwise, all that food and drink go in vain.
310.12: The donor should be conscious that the lord receives his gift with pleasure. He should confer gifts to a worthy person. If knowing thus, he donates gifts every day. Visnu is pleased thereby. Otherwise, gifts of the donor are rendered waste.
310.13: One should keep one's house decorated with the arti¬ cles of precious metal knowing that lord always likes them.
310.14: Lord Govinda abides with his sons in the house of the devotees of Vi§nu. The lord by the name of Mukunda abides in the abode of Mitra. By the name of Aniruddha he abides in the public rest house. By the name of Nariyana he abides in the house of a Br&hmana.
310.15: By the name of Hari he abides in the cowpen. By the name of Vamana he abides in the stable. By the name of Saihkar- sana he abides in Sudra. By the name of Pradyumna he abides in Vaiiya.
310.16: By the name of Janardana he abides in Ktra. By the name of Mahidasa he abides in the fisherman. By the name of Upendra he abides in the earth.
310.17: By the name of Cakrapani he abides in the elephant. By the name of Viva he abides in the heart. By the name of Bhutabhavana he abides in dogs.
310.18: By the name of Trivikrama he abides in the ant. By the name of Hari he abides in the firmament. By the name of Ananta and Hari he abides in all castes The multi-formed Hari has no class, no family, no race.
310.19: Knowing all this, Laksmana set herself to propitiate the lord. "May lord be pleased with my worship and become my husband".
310.20: Desiring Visnu to be her lord she gave up her body and was born in the country of Madras.

311.1: Thus asked by Garuda, lord Krsna, son of Devaki, spoke in a voice resembling the thunder of clouds.
311.2: Jambavatl, the daughter of Soma in her former birth, purified her life as well as her father's by the worship of Visnu,
311.3: She heard the sacred Puranas, bowed to and circum¬ ambulated Visnu who takes men across the ocean of life and death. She kept him ever in her memory.
311.4: She placed her wealth at the lotus-feet of the lord who takes men across the ocean of suffering. She set her tongue to the praise of Hari.
311.5: She applied her hands to the act of sweeping the temple of Visnu with devotion that removes impurity. She directed her ears to hearing the sacred tale of Hari—the tale that takes one to heaven or effects release.
311.6: She set her eyes to seeing the idols of Visnu—a fact that effaces impurities of body accrued from eternal times.
311.7: She set her organ of smell to the feet of Hari—the feet which give release from the circle of birth and death. She set her organ of taste to partake the remanents of what had been offered to Hari and were mixed with Tulasi leaves.
311.8: She set her feet to traversing the path sacred to Hari, her head to bowing at the feet of lord, her heart and mouth to his praise and service as is the practice among the illustrious devotees of Visnu.
311.9: She directed her intellect to thinking upon the sup¬ reme spirit, and her organ of speech to the praise of the lord.
311.10: Thus, she placed her life at the feet of the lord, started on pilgrimage with her father, to propitiate lord Visnu.
311.11: Thereafter she made a vow in the presence of the
311.12: O lord, so long I remain on pilgrimage, I shall be in Yaugic practice. May you, O lord, favour me with the company of the faithful, not with the company of non-believers.
311.13: Let me hear the narrative of Hari. May I not go on pilgrimage with friends, sons, relatives and also with those who start on journey with a set moti\T or purpose.
311.14: If one goes on pilgrimage on foot let him take the lalagrama stone with himself. Such a person obtains full fruits of his pilgrimage.
311.15: If he goes on pilgrimage on a vehicle or a horse he derives the fruit of his pilgrimage less by one half. If he goes
311.16: She took bath, washed off the ointment and listened to the Puranas. She shared food with her father and together with him set out on journey the next day. She walked the dis¬ tance of one Kosa, the very next day.
311.17: She worshipped and fed the Brahmanas and listened to the story of the lord. Those who perform journey in this way,, their journey becomes fruitful.
311.18: The noble have declared that pilgrimage without compassion is barren. Similar fate awaits those who do not hear the divine story of lord Hari on their way to a shrine.
311.19: The sin accruing from the worship of lord without devotion can be wiped off by the repeated uttering of the Vedic mantra for the purpose or by meditating upon Visnu. What¬ ever is performed by way of worship without devotion is a sheer waste. Thus say the learned devotees of Visnu.
311.20: Hence, O lord of birds, one should devote oneself to Visnu, hear his narrative which destroys sins, remember one¬ self falling at the feet of the lord, thus he should devote himself to the service of the lord.
311.21: She proceeded, O lord of birds, together with her father to visit lord Visnu, the consort of Laksnu, at the Se?a mountain. She thought of Hari all the way to the shrine.
311.22: "When shall I see lord Visnu of wide chest, adorned with Srivatsa.' When shall I see the lord with lovely belly marked with three folds.
311.23: When shall I see the lord with the neck resembling a conch and the resting-place for Maharloka. When shall I see the navel of the lord, the resort of the firmament.
311.24: When shall I see the face of the lord, the resort of the people of Janas.
311.25: When shall I see the head of the lord, the resort of Satya people. When shall I see the hips of the lord, the resort of Bhu people.
311.26: When shall I see the thigh of the lord, the resort of Talatala people.
311.27: When shall I see the tender knees of the lord, the resort of Sutala people. When shall I see the soles of the lord the resort of Patala people.
311.28: Thus pondering, on her way to the shrine, she reached the mountain Sesa where she saw lord iSesa possessed of one thousand hoods. The mountain abounded in various trees and was inhabited by monkeys.
311.29: She said: "I have seen this mountain by my merits accumulated since various births."
311.30: One should salute the lord in front of the image and not at the back. She bowed to the lord with the eight organs of her body, placing Salagrama in front.
311.31: The devotees of Visnu should act accordingly. The consort of Laksmi abides at the peak of the mountain, wor¬ shipped or honoured by Laksmf, Brahma and others.
311.32: I shall see the mighty, supreme lord of Lak|m!. I shall attend the mountain and put up my residence at the holy hermitage of Kapila.

312.2: In each and every step of the mountain the people recite Bhagavadgita remembering lord Srinivasa. They are transported to the highest region of delight. When the lord is pleased, they attain liberation. O girl, there is nothing inaccessible to a person with whom lord Hari is so pleased.
312.3: He who hears this Parana while ascending the mountain attains the merit of visiting holy places of pilgrimage. Therefore while ascending the steps the devotees should praise Hari Srinivasa and their preceptor.
312.4: She heard the glory of ascending the steps, set up and worshipped the holy Salagrama thereon and started ascending.
312.5: O lord of birds, while ascending the steps the non- Vaisnava devotees feel no pleasure. O lord of birds, this very fact is enough to put them into deep dark regions.

312.8: People do not realize the true form of lord Hari. They are swayed by tamas and rajas.
312.9: Those characterized by Sattva are seldom found in the Kali age. Those who appear to be devotees of Visnu are in fact not devotees at all. Rather, they arc busy in filling up their belly and meeting their sexual desire; for they undertake journey with that end in view.
312.10: O lord of birds, I shall tell you the nature of a true devotee. A true devotee is one who is devoid of hatred, is full of affection and possesses keen insight and devotion. I shall now tell you the forms of hate.

312.13: O sage Jaigisavya, please tell me who are the true devotees. How did they show their devotion. Lord Visnu, 3rmiva who is compassionate to devotees is indeed their protector.

313.1: At the gate of the temple of iSrInivasa she and her companions saw Svamipuskarini saying, "O lord Hari, Srinivasa", she meditated on the lord who takes Brahma and others across the ocean of existence.
313.2: There, in the pool, Visnu abides, together with other gods for the preservation of people. Hence, the pool is called Svamipuskarini. Therein, the maiden and her companions took bath.
313.3: O lord of birds, formerly, the gods purified themselves by taking bath and entered the temple of Srinivasa to practise penance with sincere devotion. As instructed by the preceptor, the maid too acted all accordingly, O lord of birds.
313.4: Then, the lord in his full and beautiful form appeared before her. The maid saw the beautiful form of Srinivasa and was delighted thereby.
313.5: Her heart overflowed with pleasure at the sight of the lord. Her eyes were full of tears and her body showed joyful signs
313.6: "O blissful lord, save me from worldly affections, grant me your eternal bliss by releasing me from the shackles of Karman.
313.7: O lord, dissociate me from my bad companions—desire wrath and greed, and destroy my strong foes, viz., the obstacles.
313.8: O lord ofLaksmi, Sarasvati, Brahma and the universe protect me; O lord ofLaksmi, the primeval course of the Uni¬ verse, whose lotus feet are bowed to by the gods, protect
313.9: Thus paying homage with reverence she praised the primeval lord. O lord of birds, there are innumerable merits n Visnu which are not known to Laksmi.
313.10: [She continued] "Unknowneven to Laksmi, there exist several qualities in Hari. I cannot praise you adequately. Still I shall try to praise you, O lord.
313.11: By the favour of Brahma, the lord of speech, by the favour of Rudra, above all by your favour, I praise you, O lord. Be kind enough to bestow peace on me.
313.12: O lord, if you are pleased with me, bestow devotion on me for your feet. At your very sight, O lord, good and evil—both disappear for ever.
313.13: I do not seek for that wealth which would make me dumb to the entreaties of the poor or the preceptor and drive me off from the service of your lotus-feet.
313.14: Please take off my learning, progeny, wealth and pride. Orant me devotion for your lotus-feet. Take off my jealousy and intolerance for the noble devotees of Visnu. O lord of Venkata grant me protection.
313.15: O primeval cause of the universe, gram me that mantra which may enable me to meet you again. I ask for nothing more than my contact with your lotus-feet. Please grant me this all if you are so pleased with me."
313.16: O maid, by this mantra you will achieve the object of your desire." Having addressed the maid thus, the lord appeared before her in a symbolic form.
313.17: The girl bowed to the lord and stayed in the vicinity of the lake named Svdmisaras. On that very day she propitiated the Brahmanas and other castes with the cooked food of ingredients.
313.18: ''To day, my body is purified, my eyes have borne fruit, my feet have gained purpose, since I have circumambulat¬ ed you, my lord.
313.19: My hands have attained the fruits of their existence since they have clapped to glorify the lord." Thus she pleased the lord by these utterances which were full of praises for the lord.
313.20: Immersed in bliss he returned to her hermitage to¬ gether with Jaigisavya. O lord of birds, those who do not go on pilgrimage thus have all their pious activities come to naught, thus say the noble.
